## Solution

A multi-tenant contact management web application whose advantage over CRM systems is simplicity. A User signs in (Firebase Authentication: email and password, or Google) and creates a **Workspace** for each project or company; only its **Members** see it, each with a **Role** (Owner, Editor, Viewer). A Workspace holds **Contacts** with fixed **Predefined fields**, free key-value **Attributes** and free **Tags** used as categories. Every change writes an immutable **Revision**, so the full history is visible and any earlier state can be **Restored**. The application finds **Duplicate sets**, warns while saving, lets an Editor **Merge** them, and **Exports** the selected or filtered Contacts to Excel. The whole system is reached through one secured REST API; the user interface is Slovenian.

The complete, fixed requirements are the project inputs in the repository: user stories US-001 to US-013, business rules BR-01 to BR-19, 87 acceptance criteria, end-to-end scenarios E2E-01 to E2E-07, the fixed API contract, architecture constraints AR-01 to AR-10, security requirements SR-01 to SR-11 (OWASP ASVS 5.0 Level 2), non-functional requirements NFR-01 to NFR-07, the glossary and ADR-0001. This spec summarises them; where they differ, the inputs win.

## User Stories

Sign-in and Users

1. As a person, I want to sign up with email and password, so that I can start using the application without a Google account.
2. As a person, I want to sign in with my Google account, so that I do not need another password.
3. As a User, I want to sign out, so that nobody else at my computer can see my contacts.
4. As a User, I want every page to require sign-in, so that an open browser tab on a shared computer does not expose contacts after sign-out.
5. As a User, I want the application to know me by my sign-in identity and keep my email and display name current, so that colleagues see who I am.
6. As a User, I want requests with a missing, malformed, expired or foreign token to be refused, so that only I can act as me.

Workspaces

7. As a User, I want to create a Workspace with a name, so that I can keep the contacts of one project or company apart from others.
8. As a User, I want to become Owner of the Workspace I create, so that I can manage it.
9. As a User, I want to see the list of Workspaces I belong to, with my Role in each, so that I can switch between projects.
10. As an Owner, I want to rename a Workspace, so that its name stays meaningful when a project changes.
11. As an Owner, I want to delete a Workspace by typing its exact name, so that a project's data can be removed completely and not by accident.
12. As a Member of a deleted Workspace, I want it to disappear from my list, so that I am not confused by data that no longer exists.

Members and invitations

13. As an Owner, I want to add a colleague by email with a Role, so that we can keep a Workspace's contacts together.
14. As an Owner, I want a colleague who already uses the application to get access immediately, so that we can start working at once.
15. As an Owner, I want to add someone who has not signed up yet, as a pending invitation, so that they get access as soon as they sign in.
16. As an invited person, I want the invitation to apply only after my email is verified, so that nobody can claim my invitation with an unverified address.
17. As an Owner, I want to cancel a pending invitation, so that a mistaken address never gets access.
18. As an Owner, I want to change a Member's Role, so that responsibilities can change over time.
19. As an Owner, I want to remove a Member, so that someone who leaves the project loses access.
20. As a Member, I want to leave a Workspace, so that it no longer appears in my list.
21. As an Owner, I want the system to always keep at least one Owner, so that a Workspace can never become unmanageable.
22. As a Member, I want to see the Workspace's Members and pending invitations, so that I know who can see our contacts.
23. As an Owner, I want adding the same person twice to be refused, so that the member list stays clean.

Isolation and Roles

24. As a Member, I want my Workspace to be invisible to everyone who is not a Member, so that our contacts stay private.
25. As a Member, I want a non-Member to be unable to tell whether my Workspace or a Contact in it even exists, so that nothing leaks through error messages.
26. As a Member, I want a Contact of my Workspace to be unreachable through another Workspace's address, so that a guessed id never exposes data.
27. As a Member of two Workspaces, I want search, Tags, Duplicate sets and Exports to stay within the Workspace I am in, so that data never mixes.
28. As a Viewer, I want to read, search and export Contacts but change nothing, so that I can use the data without risk of breaking it.
29. As an Editor, I want to change Contacts and Tags but not manage Members, so that responsibilities are clear.
30. As a Member, I want controls my Role does not allow to be hidden, so that the interface stays simple and honest.
31. As an Owner, I want refused actions to be refused by the server even if someone bypasses the interface, so that Roles really protect the data.

Contacts

32. As an Editor, I want to create a Contact with first name, last name, email, phone, company, job title, street, postal code, city, country and note, so that the Workspace holds complete contact data.
33. As an Editor, I want a Contact to need at least a first name, a last name or an email, so that empty Contacts cannot be saved.
34. As an Editor, I want leading and trailing spaces removed automatically, so that copied text does not create subtle differences.
35. As an Editor, I want invalid emails, unknown country codes and over-long values rejected with an error next to the field, so that I can correct them immediately.
36. As an Editor, I want the form to check obvious mistakes before sending, and to keep what I typed after an error, so that I never retype a form.
37. As an Editor, I want Slovenian characters (č, š, ž, Č, Š, Ž, ć, đ) kept exactly in every field, so that names are spelled correctly.
38. As an Editor, I want to change a Contact, so that its data stays current.
39. As an Editor, I want a change based on an outdated version to be refused, so that I never overwrite a colleague's change without seeing it.
40. As an Editor, I want to delete a Contact without losing it forever, so that a mistake can be undone.
41. As a Member, I want a separate view of Deleted contacts, so that I can find and restore them.

Attributes

42. As an Editor, I want to add free key-value Attributes such as `kompetenca=spletnoProgramiranje`, so that I can record what the Predefined fields do not cover.
43. As an Editor, I want Attributes kept in the order I entered them, so that the Contact reads the way I wrote it.
44. As an Editor, I want keys that are malformed, repeated (ignoring letter case) or equal to a Predefined field name refused, so that Attributes stay consistent and never shadow real fields.
45. As an Editor, I want to change or remove Attributes, so that the Contact stays accurate.

Tags

46. As an Editor, I want to label Contacts with Tags such as `neObvescaj` or `udelezenec2025` by simply typing them, so that I can categorise without setting anything up first.
47. As an Editor, I want Tags that differ only in letter case to be the same Tag, keeping the first spelling, so that categories do not split by accident.
48. As a Member, I want to see the Workspace's Tags with how many Contacts carry each, so that I understand the categories in use.
49. As an Editor, I want to rename a Tag across the whole Workspace, so that a category can be renamed in one step.
50. As an Editor, I want renaming a Tag onto an existing name refused, so that two categories never merge silently.
51. As an Editor, I want to delete a Tag from every Contact at once, so that an obsolete category disappears.
52. As a Member, I want Tag renames and deletions recorded in each affected Contact's history, so that the change is traceable.

Search and filter

53. As a Member, I want one search box that finds Contacts by name, email, phone, company or city, so that finding someone takes one step.
54. As a Member, I want search to ignore letter case and diacritics (`sasa` finds `Saša`), so that I find people however I type.
55. As a Member, I want to filter by one or more Tags, with all or any of them, so that I can work with a category.
56. As a Member, I want to filter by Attribute value or presence, so that I can find, for example, everyone with a given competence.
57. As a Member, I want to filter by country and company, combined with search, so that I can narrow down large lists.
58. As a Member, I want to sort by last name, first name, company or last change, so that the list fits my task.
59. As a Member, I want paging with the total count, so that large Workspaces stay fast and I know how many Contacts match.
60. As a Member, I want search and filters to update the list without reloading the page, so that the application feels quick.

Revisions and Restore

61. As a Member, I want to see every Revision of a Contact with who made it, when and what kind of change it was, so that I know its history.
62. As a Member, I want each Revision to show exactly which fields, Attributes and Tags changed, with old and new values, so that I understand the change at a glance.
63. As an Editor, I want to restore an earlier Revision, so that a wrong change can be undone without retyping.
64. As an Editor, I want a restore to create a new Revision rather than erase history, so that the restore itself is traceable.
65. As an Editor, I want restoring a Revision to bring back Tags that were deleted since, so that the restored state is complete.
66. As an Editor, I want to restore a Deleted contact with its last state, so that deleting is never final by mistake.
67. As a Member, I want Revisions to be impossible to change or delete, so that the audit trail can be trusted.

Duplicates and Merge

68. As a Member, I want to see sets of Contacts that are probably the same person, matched by email, phone or full name, so that I can clean up the Workspace.
69. As a Member, I want email matching to ignore case, phone matching to ignore formatting and `00`/`+`, and name matching to ignore case, extra spaces and diacritics, so that real duplicates are found.
70. As a Member, I want contacts connected through different matches (A and B by email, B and C by phone) shown as one set, so that I merge them in one go.
71. As an Editor, I want a warning, with links, when the Contact I just saved looks like an existing one, so that I notice duplicates immediately without being blocked.
72. As an Editor, I want to Merge 2 to 10 Contacts, choosing which one survives and, per differing value, which value to keep, so that the result is the best data of all.
73. As an Editor, I want Tags and Attributes of merged Contacts combined, so that no categorisation is lost.
74. As an Editor, I want merged-away Contacts kept as Deleted contacts pointing to the Survivor, so that nothing is lost and the merge is traceable.
75. As an Editor, I want a Merge to fail completely if any Contact changed meanwhile, so that I never merge stale data.

Export

76. As a Member, I want to select Contacts with checkboxes and export them to Excel, so that I can hand exactly those on.
77. As a Member, I want to export all Contacts matching my current search and filters when nothing is selected, so that exporting a category takes one click.
78. As a Member, I want the workbook to have a fixed column layout, Tags in one column and one column per Attribute key, so that it is predictable and easy to process.
79. As a Member, I want every cell to be plain text, never a formula, so that opening an export can never run anything.
80. As a Member, I want the file named after the Workspace and the date, so that exports are easy to file.
81. As a Viewer, I want to be allowed to export, so that I can use the data outside the system.

Erasure and privacy

82. As an Owner, I want to permanently erase a Deleted contact with all its Revisions, so that I can honour a person's request to have their data removed.
83. As an Owner, I want only Deleted contacts to be erasable, so that erasure is always a deliberate second step.
84. As a contact person, I want my data never written to logs, so that it does not leak through operations.

Operations

85. As an operator, I want the whole stack (frontend, backend, PostgreSQL, Auth emulator) to start with one command, so that local runs and demonstrations are simple.
86. As an operator, I want data to survive container recreation, so that an update never loses contacts.
87. As an operator, I want health and readiness endpoints used by the containers, so that a broken service is detected.
88. As an operator, I want production to refuse to start with emulator settings or a demo project id, so that test shortcuts can never reach production.
89. As a Member of a Workspace with 10,000 Contacts, I want list and search answers within half a second, so that the application stays pleasant at scale.
90. As a keyboard or screen-reader user, I want the main pages to meet accessibility rules, so that I can use the application too.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Components:** a Spring Boot backend (Java 21) and a React frontend (Vite, React Router, hand-written CSS, no component library) served by nginx, which also forwards `/api` to the backend; PostgreSQL as the only store; Firebase Authentication for sign-in, with the Firebase Auth Emulator in local and test environments; everything started by one Docker Compose file. Exact versions are fixed in the tech stack input; nothing outside it is added without a recorded decision.
- **API:** the REST API is fixed by the API contract input, and its paths, methods, field names and status codes are part of the requirements (the hidden oracle relies on them). Resources: the current User; Workspaces; Members and invitations; Contacts with Revisions, restore and purge; Tags; Duplicate sets; Merge; Export. Errors always have the shape of a list of field errors. Non-Member gets 404 indistinguishable from "does not exist"; insufficient Role gets 403; an outdated version gets 409; over the rate limit 429.
- **Tenancy (ADR-0001):** one shared schema with the Workspace id on every Workspace-owned row. Isolation lives in one Workspace-scoped access layer that receives the Workspace id and the caller's verified membership; no other code reaches the persistence of Workspace-owned data. No row-level security, no schema per Workspace. Checked by an architecture rule.
- **Authentication and authorization:** one authentication adapter verifies the Firebase ID token (signature, audience, issuer, expiry) and yields the User; no other code depends on Firebase. Authorization is the application's own: membership and Role stored in PostgreSQL, never taken from token claims or request bodies. Pending invitations become memberships at the first request with a matching verified email.
- **Revisions:** every create, update, delete, restore and merge writes exactly one immutable Revision per changed Contact, holding the full state (Predefined fields, Attributes, Tags, deleted flag), change type, author and time. The Contact's version is its latest Revision number; changes name the version they are based on (optimistic locking). A change, its Revision and the version check share one transaction; Merge and Tag rename or delete change all affected Contacts in one transaction or none.
- **Deletion:** delete is soft (Deleted contact, restorable); only an Owner's purge of a Deleted contact and Workspace deletion remove data permanently, Revisions included.
- **Duplicates:** exact matching after normalisation (email lower case; phone `00`→`+` and digits only, at least 6 digits; full name lower case, diacritics removed, whitespace collapsed), grouped transitively into Duplicate sets; Deleted contacts excluded. No fuzzy matching.
- **Search:** case- and diacritic-insensitive substring search over name, email, phone, company and city; filters by Tags (all or any), country, company and Attributes; sorting and paging all run in the database, not in memory.
- **Export:** an `.xlsx` workbook with the fixed column order of the contract, one column per Attribute key (lower case, sorted), every cell written as text; at most 10,000 Contacts per Export.
- **Schema:** evolves only through versioned database migrations.
- **Frontend:** Slovenian only, no translation framework; the API's English error messages are mapped to Slovenian texts; no secret in the frontend, its Firebase configuration comes from configuration.
- **Security level:** OWASP ASVS 5.0 Level 2 for both components, plus the project's security requirements (token verification, emulator never in production, isolation, verified-email invitations, rate and size limits, text-only export cells, server-set Revision author, no personal data in logs, text-only rendering, Host header pinning at the proxy, configured CORS).

## Testing Decisions

- **A good test checks external behaviour only:** what a caller of the REST API or a person in the browser can observe (status codes, response bodies, the workbook, what the page shows). Tests never inspect repositories, internal services or table layouts, so the internals can change freely.
- **Seam 1 (primary): the REST API.** All backend acceptance criteria are tested through HTTP against a real PostgreSQL (Testcontainers) with tokens from the Firebase Auth Emulator: Workspaces, Members, isolation (404 with the same body as a missing Workspace), Roles (403), Contacts, Attributes, Tags, search and filters, Revisions and Restore, Duplicate sets, Merge, Export (workbook read back and checked), purge, rate limits. This is the same seam the hidden oracle uses.
- **Token verification in production mode** goes through the same REST seam, with the backend's key endpoint configured to a test key instead of the emulator, covering wrong audience, wrong issuer, expiry and a bad signature (DoD-P05).
- **Seam 2: the frontend's API-client boundary.** UI criteria (field errors next to fields with values kept, the duplicate warning with links, controls hidden by Role, selection and Export, the history diff, search and filters without reload) are component tests with the API client faked.
- **Seam 3: the browser against the full stack,** exactly the seven fixed end-to-end scenarios E2E-01 to E2E-07, each also running an axe-core accessibility check on the main pages it visits. No other end-to-end tests.
- **Acceptance tests come first and are frozen** (template phase 3); unit tests are added only afterwards to reach the quality gate: line coverage ≥ 95 % and adjusted mutation score ≥ 90 % per component, over all production code.
- **Runtime demonstrations, not tests:** persistence across container recreation, health and readiness, and the 10,000-Contact response-time target.
- **Prior art:** none in this repository yet (no code). The closest prior art is the conference-registration project built with the same template: Testcontainers-based acceptance tests through MockMvc, Vitest component tests, Playwright end-to-end tests, PIT and Stryker for mutation.

## Out of Scope

- Import of Contacts from Excel, CSV, vCard or any other source (a candidate change request).
- Fuzzy or similarity-based duplicate matching; automatic merging.
- Sending any email, including invitations and notifications.
- Typed Attributes, a Workspace-wide Attribute schema, several values per Attribute key.
- Moving or copying Contacts between Workspaces; sharing a single Contact outside its Workspace.
- A Workspace-wide activity feed (a candidate change request).
- Translations other than Slovenian; multi-factor authentication; roles from identity-provider claims.
- Database-level tenant isolation (row-level security, schema per Workspace), per ADR-0001.
- An administration interface across Workspaces; mobile applications; payment.

## Further Notes

- The requirements are deliberately fixed so that agent runs are comparable: the acceptance criteria, end-to-end scenarios and API contract are inputs that the implementer does not reword, and a gap or contradiction is recorded as a decision rather than resolved silently.
- A hidden oracle outside this repository checks every finished run through the API; implementers never see it and must not try to.
- Manual checks left for a human after release: sign-up, email verification and Google sign-in against a real Firebase project; HTTPS, redirects and `/api` routing behind the production reverse proxy.
- The domain vocabulary (Workspace, Member, Role, Contact, Predefined field, Attribute, Tag, Revision, Deleted contact, Restore, Duplicate set, Merge, Survivor, Export) is defined in the glossary; avoided synonyms (group, project, tenant, record, version in prose, custom field, label, archive, master) are not used in code, API or UI.

## Parent

A User can open the application, sign up or sign in (email and password, or Google, through Firebase Authentication; the Auth emulator locally), see the list of Workspaces they belong to, create one and rename it as Owner, and sign out. The backend verifies every token itself, keeps its own User record, and reaches Workspace data only through the Workspace-scoped access layer of ADR-0001, so a non-Member gets 404. - [ ] AC-001-04: sign-up, sign-in and sign-out work in the browser; after sign-out every page shows the sign-in page

## Solution

A multi-tenant contact management web application whose advantage over CRM systems is simplicity. A User signs in (Firebase Authentication: email and password, or Google) and creates a **Workspace** for each project or company; only its **Members** see it, each with a **Role** (Owner, Editor, Viewer). A Workspace holds **Contacts** with fixed **Predefined fields**, free key-value **Attributes** and free **Tags** used as categories. Every change writes an immutable **Revision**, so the full history is visible and any earlier state can be **Restored**. The application finds **Duplicate sets**, warns while saving, lets an Editor **Merge** them, and **Exports** the selected or filtered Contacts to Excel. The whole system is reached through one secured REST API; the user interface is Slovenian.

The complete, fixed requirements are the project inputs in the repository: user stories US-001 to US-013, business rules BR-01 to BR-19, 87 acceptance criteria, end-to-end scenarios E2E-01 to E2E-07, the fixed API contract, architecture constraints AR-01 to AR-10, security requirements SR-01 to SR-11 (OWASP ASVS 5.0 Level 2), non-functional requirements NFR-01 to NFR-07, the glossary and ADR-0001. This spec summarises them; where they differ, the inputs win.

## User Stories

Sign-in and Users

1. As a person, I want to sign up with email and password, so that I can start using the application without a Google account.
2. As a person, I want to sign in with my Google account, so that I do not need another password.
3. As a User, I want to sign out, so that nobody else at my computer can see my contacts.
4. As a User, I want every page to require sign-in, so that an open browser tab on a shared computer does not expose contacts after sign-out.
5. As a User, I want the application to know me by my sign-in identity and keep my email and display name current, so that colleagues see who I am.
6. As a User, I want requests with a missing, malformed, expired or foreign token to be refused, so that only I can act as me.

Workspaces

7. As a User, I want to create a Workspace with a name, so that I can keep the contacts of one project or company apart from others.
8. As a User, I want to become Owner of the Workspace I create, so that I can manage it.
9. As a User, I want to see the list of Workspaces I belong to, with my Role in each, so that I can switch between projects.
10. As an Owner, I want to rename a Workspace, so that its name stays meaningful when a project changes.
11. As an Owner, I want to delete a Workspace by typing its exact name, so that a project's data can be removed completely and not by accident.
12. As a Member of a deleted Workspace, I want it to disappear from my list, so that I am not confused by data that no longer exists.

Members and invitations

13. As an Owner, I want to add a colleague by email with a Role, so that we can keep a Workspace's contacts together.
14. As an Owner, I want a colleague who already uses the application to get access immediately, so that we can start working at once.
15. As an Owner, I want to add someone who has not signed up yet, as a pending invitation, so that they get access as soon as they sign in.
16. As an invited person, I want the invitation to apply only after my email is verified, so that nobody can claim my invitation with an unverified address.
17. As an Owner, I want to cancel a pending invitation, so that a mistaken address never gets access.
18. As an Owner, I want to change a Member's Role, so that responsibilities can change over time.
19. As an Owner, I want to remove a Member, so that someone who leaves the project loses access.
20. As a Member, I want to leave a Workspace, so that it no longer appears in my list.
21. As an Owner, I want the system to always keep at least one Owner, so that a Workspace can never become unmanageable.
22. As a Member, I want to see the Workspace's Members and pending invitations, so that I know who can see our contacts.
23. As an Owner, I want adding the same person twice to be refused, so that the member list stays clean.

Isolation and Roles

24. As a Member, I want my Workspace to be invisible to everyone who is not a Member, so that our contacts stay private.
25. As a Member, I want a non-Member to be unable to tell whether my Workspace or a Contact in it even exists, so that nothing leaks through error messages.
26. As a Member, I want a Contact of my Workspace to be unreachable through another Workspace's address, so that a guessed id never exposes data.
27. As a Member of two Workspaces, I want search, Tags, Duplicate sets and Exports to stay within the Workspace I am in, so that data never mixes.
28. As a Viewer, I want to read, search and export Contacts but change nothing, so that I can use the data without risk of breaking it.
29. As an Editor, I want to change Contacts and Tags but not manage Members, so that responsibilities are clear.
30. As a Member, I want controls my Role does not allow to be hidden, so that the interface stays simple and honest.
31. As an Owner, I want refused actions to be refused by the server even if someone bypasses the interface, so that Roles really protect the data.

Contacts

32. As an Editor, I want to create a Contact with first name, last name, email, phone, company, job title, street, postal code, city, country and note, so that the Workspace holds complete contact data.
33. As an Editor, I want a Contact to need at least a first name, a last name or an email, so that empty Contacts cannot be saved.
34. As an Editor, I want leading and trailing spaces removed automatically, so that copied text does not create subtle differences.
35. As an Editor, I want invalid emails, unknown country codes and over-long values rejected with an error next to the field, so that I can correct them immediately.
36. As an Editor, I want the form to check obvious mistakes before sending, and to keep what I typed after an error, so that I never retype a form.
37. As an Editor, I want Slovenian characters (č, š, ž, Č, Š, Ž, ć, đ) kept exactly in every field, so that names are spelled correctly.
38. As an Editor, I want to change a Contact, so that its data stays current.
39. As an Editor, I want a change based on an outdated version to be refused, so that I never overwrite a colleague's change without seeing it.
40. As an Editor, I want to delete a Contact without losing it forever, so that a mistake can be undone.
41. As a Member, I want a separate view of Deleted contacts, so that I can find and restore them.

Attributes

42. As an Editor, I want to add free key-value Attributes such as `kompetenca=spletnoProgramiranje`, so that I can record what the Predefined fields do not cover.
43. As an Editor, I want Attributes kept in the order I entered them, so that the Contact reads the way I wrote it.
44. As an Editor, I want keys that are malformed, repeated (ignoring letter case) or equal to a Predefined field name refused, so that Attributes stay consistent and never shadow real fields.
45. As an Editor, I want to change or remove Attributes, so that the Contact stays accurate.

Tags

46. As an Editor, I want to label Contacts with Tags such as `neObvescaj` or `udelezenec2025` by simply typing them, so that I can categorise without setting anything up first.
47. As an Editor, I want Tags that differ only in letter case to be the same Tag, keeping the first spelling, so that categories do not split by accident.
48. As a Member, I want to see the Workspace's Tags with how many Contacts carry each, so that I understand the categories in use.
49. As an Editor, I want to rename a Tag across the whole Workspace, so that a category can be renamed in one step.
50. As an Editor, I want renaming a Tag onto an existing name refused, so that two categories never merge silently.
51. As an Editor, I want to delete a Tag from every Contact at once, so that an obsolete category disappears.
52. As a Member, I want Tag renames and deletions recorded in each affected Contact's history, so that the change is traceable.

Search and filter

53. As a Member, I want one search box that finds Contacts by name, email, phone, company or city, so that finding someone takes one step.
54. As a Member, I want search to ignore letter case and diacritics (`sasa` finds `Saša`), so that I find people however I type.
55. As a Member, I want to filter by one or more Tags, with all or any of them, so that I can work with a category.
56. As a Member, I want to filter by Attribute value or presence, so that I can find, for example, everyone with a given competence.
57. As a Member, I want to filter by country and company, combined with search, so that I can narrow down large lists.
58. As a Member, I want to sort by last name, first name, company or last change, so that the list fits my task.
59. As a Member, I want paging with the total count, so that large Workspaces stay fast and I know how many Contacts match.
60. As a Member, I want search and filters to update the list without reloading the page, so that the application feels quick.

Revisions and Restore

61. As a Member, I want to see every Revision of a Contact with who made it, when and what kind of change it was, so that I know its history.
62. As a Member, I want each Revision to show exactly which fields, Attributes and Tags changed, with old and new values, so that I understand the change at a glance.
63. As an Editor, I want to restore an earlier Revision, so that a wrong change can be undone without retyping.
64. As an Editor, I want a restore to create a new Revision rather than erase history, so that the restore itself is traceable.
65. As an Editor, I want restoring a Revision to bring back Tags that were deleted since, so that the restored state is complete.
66. As an Editor, I want to restore a Deleted contact with its last state, so that deleting is never final by mistake.
67. As a Member, I want Revisions to be impossible to change or delete, so that the audit trail can be trusted.

Duplicates and Merge

68. As a Member, I want to see sets of Contacts that are probably the same person, matched by email, phone or full name, so that I can clean up the Workspace.
69. As a Member, I want email matching to ignore case, phone matching to ignore formatting and `00`/`+`, and name matching to ignore case, extra spaces and diacritics, so that real duplicates are found.
70. As a Member, I want contacts connected through different matches (A and B by email, B and C by phone) shown as one set, so that I merge them in one go.
71. As an Editor, I want a warning, with links, when the Contact I just saved looks like an existing one, so that I notice duplicates immediately without being blocked.
72. As an Editor, I want to Merge 2 to 10 Contacts, choosing which one survives and, per differing value, which value to keep, so that the result is the best data of all.
73. As an Editor, I want Tags and Attributes of merged Contacts combined, so that no categorisation is lost.
74. As an Editor, I want merged-away Contacts kept as Deleted contacts pointing to the Survivor, so that nothing is lost and the merge is traceable.
75. As an Editor, I want a Merge to fail completely if any Contact changed meanwhile, so that I never merge stale data.

Export

76. As a Member, I want to select Contacts with checkboxes and export them to Excel, so that I can hand exactly those on.
77. As a Member, I want to export all Contacts matching my current search and filters when nothing is selected, so that exporting a category takes one click.
78. As a Member, I want the workbook to have a fixed column layout, Tags in one column and one column per Attribute key, so that it is predictable and easy to process.
79. As a Member, I want every cell to be plain text, never a formula, so that opening an export can never run anything.
80. As a Member, I want the file named after the Workspace and the date, so that exports are easy to file.
81. As a Viewer, I want to be allowed to export, so that I can use the data outside the system.

Erasure and privacy

82. As an Owner, I want to permanently erase a Deleted contact with all its Revisions, so that I can honour a person's request to have their data removed.
83. As an Owner, I want only Deleted contacts to be erasable, so that erasure is always a deliberate second step.
84. As a contact person, I want my data never written to logs, so that it does not leak through operations.

Operations

85. As an operator, I want the whole stack (frontend, backend, PostgreSQL, Auth emulator) to start with one command, so that local runs and demonstrations are simple.
86. As an operator, I want data to survive container recreation, so that an update never loses contacts.
87. As an operator, I want health and readiness endpoints used by the containers, so that a broken service is detected.
88. As an operator, I want production to refuse to start with emulator settings or a demo project id, so that test shortcuts can never reach production.
89. As a Member of a Workspace with 10,000 Contacts, I want list and search answers within half a second, so that the application stays pleasant at scale.
90. As a keyboard or screen-reader user, I want the main pages to meet accessibility rules, so that I can use the application too.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Components:** a Spring Boot backend (Java 21) and a React frontend (Vite, React Router, hand-written CSS, no component library) served by nginx, which also forwards `/api` to the backend; PostgreSQL as the only store; Firebase Authentication for sign-in, with the Firebase Auth Emulator in local and test environments; everything started by one Docker Compose file. Exact versions are fixed in the tech stack input; nothing outside it is added without a recorded decision.
- **API:** the REST API is fixed by the API contract input, and its paths, methods, field names and status codes are part of the requirements (the hidden oracle relies on them). Resources: the current User; Workspaces; Members and invitations; Contacts with Revisions, restore and purge; Tags; Duplicate sets; Merge; Export. Errors always have the shape of a list of field errors. Non-Member gets 404 indistinguishable from "does not exist"; insufficient Role gets 403; an outdated version gets 409; over the rate limit 429.
- **Tenancy (ADR-0001):** one shared schema with the Workspace id on every Workspace-owned row. Isolation lives in one Workspace-scoped access layer that receives the Workspace id and the caller's verified membership; no other code reaches the persistence of Workspace-owned data. No row-level security, no schema per Workspace. Checked by an architecture rule.
- **Authentication and authorization:** one authentication adapter verifies the Firebase ID token (signature, audience, issuer, expiry) and yields the User; no other code depends on Firebase. Authorization is the application's own: membership and Role stored in PostgreSQL, never taken from token claims or request bodies. Pending invitations become memberships at the first request with a matching verified email.
- **Revisions:** every create, update, delete, restore and merge writes exactly one immutable Revision per changed Contact, holding the full state (Predefined fields, Attributes, Tags, deleted flag), change type, author and time. The Contact's version is its latest Revision number; changes name the version they are based on (optimistic locking). A change, its Revision and the version check share one transaction; Merge and Tag rename or delete change all affected Contacts in one transaction or none.
- **Deletion:** delete is soft (Deleted contact, restorable); only an Owner's purge of a Deleted contact and Workspace deletion remove data permanently, Revisions included.
- **Duplicates:** exact matching after normalisation (email lower case; phone `00`→`+` and digits only, at least 6 digits; full name lower case, diacritics removed, whitespace collapsed), grouped transitively into Duplicate sets; Deleted contacts excluded. No fuzzy matching.
- **Search:** case- and diacritic-insensitive substring search over name, email, phone, company and city; filters by Tags (all or any), country, company and Attributes; sorting and paging all run in the database, not in memory.
- **Export:** an `.xlsx` workbook with the fixed column order of the contract, one column per Attribute key (lower case, sorted), every cell written as text; at most 10,000 Contacts per Export.
- **Schema:** evolves only through versioned database migrations.
- **Frontend:** Slovenian only, no translation framework; the API's English error messages are mapped to Slovenian texts; no secret in the frontend, its Firebase configuration comes from configuration.
- **Security level:** OWASP ASVS 5.0 Level 2 for both components, plus the project's security requirements (token verification, emulator never in production, isolation, verified-email invitations, rate and size limits, text-only export cells, server-set Revision author, no personal data in logs, text-only rendering, Host header pinning at the proxy, configured CORS).

## Testing Decisions

- **A good test checks external behaviour only:** what a caller of the REST API or a person in the browser can observe (status codes, response bodies, the workbook, what the page shows). Tests never inspect repositories, internal services or table layouts, so the internals can change freely.
- **Seam 1 (primary): the REST API.** All backend acceptance criteria are tested through HTTP against a real PostgreSQL (Testcontainers) with tokens from the Firebase Auth Emulator: Workspaces, Members, isolation (404 with the same body as a missing Workspace), Roles (403), Contacts, Attributes, Tags, search and filters, Revisions and Restore, Duplicate sets, Merge, Export (workbook read back and checked), purge, rate limits. This is the same seam the hidden oracle uses.
- **Token verification in production mode** goes through the same REST seam, with the backend's key endpoint configured to a test key instead of the emulator, covering wrong audience, wrong issuer, expiry and a bad signature (DoD-P05).
- **Seam 2: the frontend's API-client boundary.** UI criteria (field errors next to fields with values kept, the duplicate warning with links, controls hidden by Role, selection and Export, the history diff, search and filters without reload) are component tests with the API client faked.
- **Seam 3: the browser against the full stack,** exactly the seven fixed end-to-end scenarios E2E-01 to E2E-07, each also running an axe-core accessibility check on the main pages it visits. No other end-to-end tests.
- **Acceptance tests come first and are frozen** (template phase 3); unit tests are added only afterwards to reach the quality gate: line coverage ≥ 95 % and adjusted mutation score ≥ 90 % per component, over all production code.
- **Runtime demonstrations, not tests:** persistence across container recreation, health and readiness, and the 10,000-Contact response-time target.
- **Prior art:** none in this repository yet (no code). The closest prior art is the conference-registration project built with the same template: Testcontainers-based acceptance tests through MockMvc, Vitest component tests, Playwright end-to-end tests, PIT and Stryker for mutation.

## Out of Scope

- Import of Contacts from Excel, CSV, vCard or any other source (a candidate change request).
- Fuzzy or similarity-based duplicate matching; automatic merging.
- Sending any email, including invitations and notifications.
- Typed Attributes, a Workspace-wide Attribute schema, several values per Attribute key.
- Moving or copying Contacts between Workspaces; sharing a single Contact outside its Workspace.
- A Workspace-wide activity feed (a candidate change request).
- Translations other than Slovenian; multi-factor authentication; roles from identity-provider claims.
- Database-level tenant isolation (row-level security, schema per Workspace), per ADR-0001.
- An administration interface across Workspaces; mobile applications; payment.

## Further Notes

- The requirements are deliberately fixed so that agent runs are comparable: the acceptance criteria, end-to-end scenarios and API contract are inputs that the implementer does not reword, and a gap or contradiction is recorded as a decision rather than resolved silently.
- A hidden oracle outside this repository checks every finished run through the API; implementers never see it and must not try to.
- Manual checks left for a human after release: sign-up, email verification and Google sign-in against a real Firebase project; HTTPS, redirects and `/api` routing behind the production reverse proxy.
- The domain vocabulary (Workspace, Member, Role, Contact, Predefined field, Attribute, Tag, Revision, Deleted contact, Restore, Duplicate set, Merge, Survivor, Export) is defined in the glossary; avoided synonyms (group, project, tenant, record, version in prose, custom field, label, archive, master) are not used in code, API or UI.

## Parent

## What to build

A User can open the application, sign up or sign in (email and password, or Google, through Firebase Authentication; the Auth emulator locally), see the list of Workspaces they belong to, create one and rename it as Owner, and sign out. The whole stack (frontend, backend, PostgreSQL, Auth emulator) starts with one Compose command. The backend verifies every token itself, keeps its own User record, and reaches Workspace data only through the Workspace-scoped access layer of ADR-0001, so a non-Member gets 404. 1	## Problem Statement
2	
3	People who work with many contacts on a project or in a company keep them in spreadsheets, mailboxes or heavyweight CRM systems. Spreadsheets get copied around, nobody knows who changed what, the same person appears three times with slightly different data, and there is no way to give a colleague access to one project's contacts without giving them everything. CRM systems solve this but are too complex for a team that only wants to keep, find, label and hand on contacts.
4	
5	## Solution
6	
7	A multi-tenant contact management web application whose advantage over CRM systems is simplicity. A User signs in (Firebase Authentication: email and password, or Google) and creates a **Workspace** for each project or company; only its **Members** see it, each with a **Role** (Owner, Editor, Viewer). A Workspace holds **Contacts** with fixed **Predefined fields**, free key-value **Attributes** and free **Tags** used as categories. Every change writes an immutable **Revision**, so the full history is visible and any earlier state can be **Restored**. The application finds **Duplicate sets**, warns while saving, lets an Editor **Merge** them, and **Exports** the selected or filtered Contacts to Excel. The whole system is reached through one secured REST API; the user interface is Slovenian.
8	
9	The complete, fixed requirements are the project inputs in the repository: user stories US-001 to US-013, business rules BR-01 to BR-19, 87 acceptance criteria, end-to-end scenarios E2E-01 to E2E-07, the fixed API contract, architecture constraints AR-01 to AR-10, security requirements SR-01 to SR-11 (OWASP ASVS 5.0 Level 2), non-functional requirements NFR-01 to NFR-07, the glossary and ADR-0001. This spec summarises them; where they differ, the inputs win.
10	
11	## User Stories
12	
13	Sign-in and Users
14	
15	1. As a person, I want to sign up with email and password, so that I can start using the application without a Google account.
16	2. As a person, I want to sign in with my Google account, so that I do not need another password.
17	3. As a User, I want to sign out, so that nobody else at my computer can see my contacts.
18	4. As a User, I want every page to require sign-in, so that an open browser tab on a shared computer does not expose contacts after sign-out.
19	5. As a User, I want the application to know me by my sign-in identity and keep my email and display name current, so that colleagues see who I am.
20	6. As a User, I want requests with a missing, malformed, expired or foreign token to be refused, so that only I can act as me.
21	
22	Workspaces
23	
24	7. As a User, I want to create a Workspace with a name, so that I can keep the contacts of one project or company apart from others.
25	8. As a User, I want to become Owner of the Workspace I create, so that I can manage it.
26	9. As a User, I want to see the list of Workspaces I belong to, with my Role in each, so that I can switch between projects.
27	10. As an Owner, I want to rename a Workspace, so that its name stays meaningful when a project changes.
28	11. As an Owner, I want to delete a Workspace by typing its exact name, so that a project's data can be removed completely and not by accident.
29	12. As a Member of a deleted Workspace, I want it to disappear from my list, so that I am not confused by data that no longer exists.
30	
31	Members and invitations
32	
33	13. As an Owner, I want to add a colleague by email with a Role, so that we can keep a Workspace's contacts together.
34	14. As an Owner, I want a colleague who already uses the application to get access immediately, so that we can start working at once.
35	15. As an Owner, I want to add someone who has not signed up yet, as a pending invitation, so that they get access as soon as they sign in.
36	16. As an invited person, I want the invitation to apply only after my email is verified, so that nobody can claim my invitation with an unverified address.
37	17. As an Owner, I want to cancel a pending invitation, so that a mistaken address never gets access.
38	18. As an Owner, I want to change a Member's Role, so that responsibilities can change over time.
39	19. As an Owner, I want to remove a Member, so that someone who leaves the project loses access.
40	20. As a Member, I want to leave a Workspace, so that it no longer appears in my list.
41	21. As an Owner, I want the system to always keep at least one Owner, so that a Workspace can never become unmanageable.
42	22. As a Member, I want to see the Workspace's Members and pending invitations, so that I know who can see our contacts.
43	23. As an Owner, I want adding the same person twice to be refused, so that the member list stays clean.
44	
45	Isolation and Roles
46	
47	24. As a Member, I want my Workspace to be invisible to everyone who is not a Member, so that our contacts stay private.
48	25. As a Member, I want a non-Member to be unable to tell whether my Workspace or a Contact in it even exists, so that nothing leaks through error messages.
49	26. As a Member, I want a Contact of my Workspace to be unreachable through another Workspace's address, so that a guessed id never exposes data.
50	27. As a Member of two Workspaces, I want search, Tags, Duplicate sets and Exports to stay within the Workspace I am in, so that data never mixes.
51	28. As a Viewer, I want to read, search and export Contacts but change nothing, so that I can use the data without risk of breaking it.
52	29. As an Editor, I want to change Contacts and Tags but not manage Members, so that responsibilities are clear.
53	30. As a Member, I want controls my Role does not allow to be hidden, so that the interface stays simple and honest.
54	31. As an Owner, I want refused actions to be refused by the server even if someone bypasses the interface, so that Roles really protect the data.
55	
56	Contacts
57	
58	32. As an Editor, I want to create a Contact with first name, last name, email, phone, company, job title, street, postal code, city, country and note, so that the Workspace holds complete contact data.
59	33. As an Editor, I want a Contact to need at least a first name, a last name or an email, so that empty Contacts cannot be saved.
60	34. As an Editor, I want leading and trailing spaces removed automatically, so that copied text does not create subtle differences.
61	35. As an Editor, I want invalid emails, unknown country codes and over-long values rejected with an error next to the field, so that I can correct them immediately.
62	36. As an Editor, I want the form to check obvious mistakes before sending, and to keep what I typed after an error, so that I never retype a form.
63	37. As an Editor, I want Slovenian characters (č, š, ž, Č, Š, Ž, ć, đ) kept exactly in every field, so that names are spelled correctly.
64	38. As an Editor, I want to change a Contact, so that its data stays current.
65	39. As an Editor, I want a change based on an outdated version to be refused, so that I never overwrite a colleague's change without seeing it.
66	40. As an Editor, I want to delete a Contact without losing it forever, so that a mistake can be undone.
67	41. As a Member, I want a separate view of Deleted contacts, so that I can find and restore them.
68	
69	Attributes
70	
71	42. As an Editor, I want to add free key-value Attributes such as `kompetenca=spletnoProgramiranje`, so that I can record what the Predefined fields do not cover.
72	43. As an Editor, I want Attributes kept in the order I entered them, so that the Contact reads the way I wrote it.
73	44. As an Editor, I want keys that are malformed, repeated (ignoring letter case) or equal to a Predefined field name refused, so that Attributes stay consistent and never shadow real fields.
74	45. As an Editor, I want to change or remove Attributes, so that the Contact stays accurate.
75	
76	Tags
77	
78	46. As an Editor, I want to label Contacts with Tags such as `neObvescaj` or `udelezenec2025` by simply typing them, so that I can categorise without setting anything up first.
79	47. As an Editor, I want Tags that differ only in letter case to be the same Tag, keeping the first spelling, so that categories do not split by accident.
80	48. As a Member, I want to see the Workspace's Tags with how many Contacts carry each, so that I understand the categories in use.
81	49. As an Editor, I want to rename a Tag across the whole Workspace, so that a category can be renamed in one step.
82	50. As an Editor, I want renaming a Tag onto an existing name refused, so that two categories never merge silently.
83	51. As an Editor, I want to delete a Tag from every Contact at once, so that an obsolete category disappears.
84	52. As a Member, I want Tag renames and deletions recorded in each affected Contact's history, so that the change is traceable.
85	
86	Search and filter
87	
88	53. As a Member, I want one search box that finds Contacts by name, email, phone, company or city, so that finding someone takes one step.
89	54. As a Member, I want search to ignore letter case and diacritics (`sasa` finds `Saša`), so that I find people however I type.
90	55. As a Member, I want to filter by one or more Tags, with all or any of them, so that I can work with a category.
91	56. As a Member, I want to filter by Attribute value or presence, so that I can find, for example, everyone with a given competence.
92	57. As a Member, I want to filter by country and company, combined with search, so that I can narrow down large lists.
93	58. As a Member, I want to sort by last name, first name, company or last change, so that the list fits my task.
94	59. As a Member, I want paging with the total count, so that large Workspaces stay fast and I know how many Contacts match.
95	60. As a Member, I want search and filters to update the list without reloading the page, so that the application feels quick.
96	
97	Revisions and Restore
98	
99	61. As a Member, I want to see every Revision of a Contact with who made it, when and what kind of change it was, so that I know its history.
100	62. As a Member, I want each Revision to show exactly which fields, Attributes and Tags changed, with old and new values, so that I understand the change at a glance.
101	63. As an Editor, I want to restore an earlier Revision, so that a wrong change can be undone without retyping.
102	64. As an Editor, I want a restore to create a new Revision rather than erase history, so that the restore itself is traceable.
103	65. As an Editor, I want restoring a Revision to bring back Tags that were deleted since, so that the restored state is complete.
104	66. As an Editor, I want to restore a Deleted contact with its last state, so that deleting is never final by mistake.
105	67. As a Member, I want Revisions to be impossible to change or delete, so that the audit trail can be trusted.
106	
107	Duplicates and Merge
108	
109	68. As a Member, I want to see sets of Contacts that are probably the same person, matched by email, phone or full name, so that I can clean up the Workspace.
110	69. As a Member, I want email matching to ignore case, phone matching to ignore formatting and `00`/`+`, and name matching to ignore case, extra spaces and diacritics, so that real duplicates are found.
111	70. As a Member, I want contacts connected through different matches (A and B by email, B and C by phone) shown as one set, so that I merge them in one go.
112	71. As an Editor, I want a warning, with links, when the Contact I just saved looks like an existing one, so that I notice duplicates immediately without being blocked.
113	72. As an Editor, I want to Merge 2 to 10 Contacts, choosing which one survives and, per differing value, which value to keep, so that the result is the best data of all.
114	73. As an Editor, I want Tags and Attributes of merged Contacts combined, so that no categorisation is lost.
115	74. As an Editor, I want merged-away Contacts kept as Deleted contacts pointing to the Survivor, so that nothing is lost and the merge is traceable.
116	75. As an Editor, I want a Merge to fail completely if any Contact changed meanwhile, so that I never merge stale data.
117	
118	Export
119	
120	76. As a Member, I want to select Contacts with checkboxes and export them to Excel, so that I can hand exactly those on.
121	77. As a Member, I want to export all Contacts matching my current search and filters when nothing is selected, so that exporting a category takes one click.
122	78. As a Member, I want the workbook to have a fixed column layout, Tags in one column and one column per Attribute key, so that it is predictable and easy to process.
123	79. As a Member, I want every cell to be plain text, never a formula, so that opening an export can never run anything.
124	80. As a Member, I want the file named after the Workspace and the date, so that exports are easy to file.
125	81. As a Viewer, I want to be allowed to export, so that I can use the data outside the system.
126	
127	Erasure and privacy
128	
129	82. As an Owner, I want to permanently erase a Deleted contact with all its Revisions, so that I can honour a person's request to have their data removed.
130	83. As an Owner, I want only Deleted contacts to be erasable, so that erasure is always a deliberate second step.
131	84. As a contact person, I want my data never written to logs, so that it does not leak through operations.
132	
133	Operations
134	
135	85. As an operator, I want the whole stack (frontend, backend, PostgreSQL, Auth emulator) to start with one command, so that local runs and demonstrations are simple.
136	86. As an operator, I want data to survive container recreation, so that an update never loses contacts.
137	87. As an operator, I want health and readiness endpoints used by the containers, so that a broken service is detected.
138	88. As an operator, I want production to refuse to start with emulator settings or a demo project id, so that test shortcuts can never reach production.
139	89. As a Member of a Workspace with 10,000 Contacts, I want list and search answers within half a second, so that the application stays pleasant at scale.
140	90. As a keyboard or screen-reader user, I want the main pages to meet accessibility rules, so that I can use the application too.
141	
142	## Implementation Decisions
143	
144	- **Components:** a Spring Boot backend (Java 21) and a React frontend (Vite, React Router, hand-written CSS, no component library) served by nginx, which also forwards `/api` to the backend; PostgreSQL as the only store; Firebase Authentication for sign-in, with the Firebase Auth Emulator in local and test environments; everything started by one Docker Compose file. Exact versions are fixed in the tech stack input; nothing outside it is added without a recorded decision.
145	- **API:** the REST API is fixed by the API contract input, and its paths, methods, field names and status codes are part of the requirements (the hidden oracle relies on them). Resources: the current User; Workspaces; Members and invitations; Contacts with Revisions, restore and purge; Tags; Duplicate sets; Merge; Export. Errors always have the shape of a list of field errors. Non-Member gets 404 indistinguishable from "does not exist"; insufficient Role gets 403; an outdated version gets 409; over the rate limit 429.
146	- **Tenancy (ADR-0001):** one shared schema with the Workspace id on every Workspace-owned row. Isolation lives in one Workspace-scoped access layer that receives the Workspace id and the caller's verified membership; no other code reaches the persistence of Workspace-owned data. No row-level security, no schema per Workspace. Checked by an architecture rule.
147	- **Authentication and authorization:** one authentication adapter verifies the Firebase ID token (signature, audience, issuer, expiry) and yields the User; no other code depends on Firebase. Authorization is the application's own: membership and Role stored in PostgreSQL, never taken from token claims or request bodies. Pending invitations become memberships at the first request with a matching verified email.
148	- **Revisions:** every create, update, delete, restore and merge writes exactly one immutable Revision per changed Contact, holding the full state (Predefined fields, Attributes, Tags, deleted flag), change type, author and time. The Contact's version is its latest Revision number; changes name the version they are based on (optimistic locking). A change, its Revision and the version check share one transaction; Merge and Tag rename or delete change all affected Contacts in one transaction or none.
149	- **Deletion:** delete is soft (Deleted contact, restorable); only an Owner's purge of a Deleted contact and Workspace deletion remove data permanently, Revisions included.
150	- **Duplicates:** exact matching after normalisation (email lower case; phone `00`→`+` and digits only, at least 6 digits; full name lower case, diacritics removed, whitespace collapsed), grouped transitively into Duplicate sets; Deleted contacts excluded. No fuzzy matching.
151	- **Search:** case- and diacritic-insensitive substring search over name, email, phone, company and city; filters by Tags (all or any), country, company and Attributes; sorting and paging all run in the database, not in memory.
152	- **Export:** an `.xlsx` workbook with the fixed column order of the contract, one column per Attribute key (lower case, sorted), every cell written as text; at most 10,000 Contacts per Export.
153	- **Schema:** evolves only through versioned database migrations.
154	- **Frontend:** Slovenian only, no translation framework; the API's English error messages are mapped to Slovenian texts; no secret in the frontend, its Firebase configuration comes from configuration.
155	- **Security level:** OWASP ASVS 5.0 Level 2 for both components, plus the project's security requirements (token verification, emulator never in production, isolation, verified-email invitations, rate and size limits, text-only export cells, server-set Revision author, no personal data in logs, text-only rendering, Host header pinning at the proxy, configured CORS).
156	
157	## Testing Decisions
158	
159	- **A good test checks external behaviour only:** what a caller of the REST API or a person in the browser can observe (status codes, response bodies, the workbook, what the page shows). Tests never inspect repositories, internal services or table layouts, so the internals can change freely.
160	- **Seam 1 (primary): the REST API.** All backend acceptance criteria are tested through HTTP against a real PostgreSQL (Testcontainers) with tokens from the Firebase Auth Emulator: Workspaces, Members, isolation (404 with the same body as a missing Workspace), Roles (403), Contacts, Attributes, Tags, search and filters, Revisions and Restore, Duplicate sets, Merge, Export (workbook read back and checked), purge, rate limits. This is the same seam the hidden oracle uses.
161	- **Token verification in production mode** goes through the same REST seam, with the backend's key endpoint configured to a test key instead of the emulator, covering wrong audience, wrong issuer, expiry and a bad signature (DoD-P05).
162	- **Seam 2: the frontend's API-client boundary.** UI criteria (field errors next to fields with values kept, the duplicate warning with links, controls hidden by Role, selection and Export, the history diff, search and filters without reload) are component tests with the API client faked.
163	- **Seam 3: the browser against the full stack,** exactly the seven fixed end-to-end scenarios E2E-01 to E2E-07, each also running an axe-core accessibility check on the main pages it visits. No other end-to-end tests.
164	- **Acceptance tests come first and are frozen** (template phase 3); unit tests are added only afterwards to reach the quality gate: line coverage ≥ 95 % and adjusted mutation score ≥ 90 % per component, over all production code.
165	- **Runtime demonstrations, not tests:** persistence across container recreation, health and readiness, and the 10,000-Contact response-time target.
166	- **Prior art:** none in this repository yet (no code). The closest prior art is the conference-registration project built with the same template: Testcontainers-based acceptance tests through MockMvc, Vitest component tests, Playwright end-to-end tests, PIT and Stryker for mutation.
167	
168	## Out of Scope
169	
170	- Import of Contacts from Excel, CSV, vCard or any other source (a candidate change request).
171	- Fuzzy or similarity-based duplicate matching; automatic merging.
172	- Sending any email, including invitations and notifications.
173	- Typed Attributes, a Workspace-wide Attribute schema, several values per Attribute key.
174	- Moving or copying Contacts between Workspaces; sharing a single Contact outside its Workspace.
175	- A Workspace-wide activity feed (a candidate change request).
176	- Translations other than Slovenian; multi-factor authentication; roles from identity-provider claims.
177	- Database-level tenant isolation (row-level security, schema per Workspace), per ADR-0001.
178	- An administration interface across Workspaces; mobile applications; payment.
179	
180	## Further Notes
181	
182	- The requirements are deliberately fixed so that agent runs are comparable: the acceptance criteria, end-to-end scenarios and API contract are inputs that the implementer does not reword, and a gap or contradiction is recorded as a decision rather than resolved silently.
183	- A hidden oracle outside this repository checks every finished run through the API; implementers never see it and must not try to.
184	- Manual checks left for a human after release: sign-up, email verification and Google sign-in against a real Firebase project; HTTPS, redirects and `/api` routing behind the production reverse proxy.
185	- The domain vocabulary (Workspace, Member, Role, Contact, Predefined field, Attribute, Tag, Revision, Deleted contact, Restore, Duplicate set, Merge, Survivor, Export) is defined in the glossary; avoided synonyms (group, project, tenant, record, version in prose, custom field, label, archive, master) are not used in code, API or UI.
186	
187	### #2 Walking skeleton: sign in and see my Workspaces
188	## Parent

192	## What to build

229	### #4 Contacts with Predefined fields, Revisions and version checks

234	## What to build
