## Problem Statement

People who work with many contacts on a project or in a company keep them in spreadsheets, mailboxes or heavyweight CRM systems. Spreadsheets get copied around, nobody knows who changed what, the same person appears three times with slightly different data, and there is no way to give a colleague access to one project's contacts without giving them everything. CRM systems solve this but are too complex for a team that only wants to keep, find, label and hand on contacts.

## Solution

A multi-tenant contact management web application whose advantage over CRM systems is simplicity. A User signs in (Firebase Authentication: email and password, or Google) and creates a **Workspace** for each project or company; only its **Members** see it, each with a **Role** (Owner, Editor, Viewer). A Workspace holds **Contacts** with fixed **Predefined fields**, free key-value **Attributes** and free **Tags** used as categories. Every change writes an immutable **Revision**, so the full history is visible and any earlier state can be **Restored**. The application finds **Duplicate sets**, warns while saving, lets an Editor **Merge** them, and **Exports** the selected or filtered Contacts to Excel. The whole system is reached through one secured REST API; the user interface is Slovenian.

The complete, fixed requirements are the project inputs in the repository: user stories US-001 to US-013, business rules BR-01 to BR-19, 87 acceptance criteria, end-to-end scenarios E2E-01 to E2E-07, the fixed API contract, architecture constraints AR-01 to AR-10, security requirements SR-01 to SR-11 (OWASP ASVS 5.0 Level 2), non-functional requirements NFR-01 to NFR-07, the glossary and ADR-0001. This spec summarises them; where they differ, the inputs win.

## User Stories

Sign-in and Users

1. As a person, I want to sign up with email and password, so that I can start using the application without a Google account.
2. As a person, I want to sign in with my Google account, so that I do not need another password.
3. As a User, I want to sign out, so that nobody else at my computer can see my contacts.
4. As a User, I want every page to require sign-in, so that an open browser tab on a shared computer does not expose contacts after sign-out.
5. As a User, I want the application to know me by my sign-in identity and keep my email and display name current, so that colleagues see who I am.
6. As a User, I want requests with a missing, malformed, expired or foreign token to be refused, so that only I can act as me.

Workspaces

7. As a User, I want to create a Workspace with a name, so that I can keep the contacts of one project or company apart from others.
8. As a User, I want to become Owner of the Workspace I create, so that I can manage it.
9. As a User, I want to see the list of Workspaces I belong to, with my Role in each, so that I can switch between projects.
10. As an Owner, I want to rename a Workspace, so that its name stays meaningful when a project changes.
11. As an Owner, I want to delete a Workspace by typing its exact name, so that a project's data can be removed completely and not by accident.
12. As a Member of a deleted Workspace, I want it to disappear from my list, so that I am not confused by data that no longer exists.

Members and invitations

13. As an Owner, I want to add a colleague by email with a Role, so that we can keep a Workspace's contacts together.
14. As an Owner, I want a colleague who already uses the application to get access immediately, so that we can start working at once.
15. As an Owner, I want to add someone who has not signed up yet, as a pending invitation, so that they get access as soon as they sign in.
16. As an invited person, I want the invitation to apply only after my email is verified, so that nobody can claim my invitation with an unverified address.
17. As an Owner, I want to cancel a pending invitation, so that a mistaken address never gets access.
18. As an Owner, I want to change a Member's Role, so that responsibilities can change over time.
19. As an Owner, I want to remove a Member, so that someone who leaves the project loses access.
20. As a Member, I want to leave a Workspace, so that it no longer appears in my list.
21. As an Owner, I want the system to always keep at least one Owner, so that a Workspace can never become unmanageable.
22. As a Member, I want to see the Workspace's Members and pending invitations, so that I know who can see our contacts.
23. As an Owner, I want adding the same person twice to be refused, so that the member list stays clean.

Isolation and Roles

24. As a Member, I want my Workspace to be invisible to everyone who is not a Member, so that our contacts stay private.
25. As a Member, I want a non-Member to be unable to tell whether my Workspace or a Contact in it even exists, so that nothing leaks through error messages.
26. As a Member, I want a Contact of my Workspace to be unreachable through another Workspace's address, so that a guessed id never exposes data.
27. As a Member of two Workspaces, I want search, Tags, Duplicate sets and Exports to stay within the Workspace I am in, so that data never mixes.
28. As a Viewer, I want to read, search and export Contacts but change nothing, so that I can use the data without risk of breaking it.
29. As an Editor, I want to change Contacts and Tags but not manage Members, so that responsibilities are clear.
30. As a Member, I want controls my Role does not allow to be hidden, so that the interface stays simple and honest.
31. As an Owner, I want refused actions to be refused by the server even if someone bypasses the interface, so that Roles really protect the data.

Contacts

32. As an Editor, I want to create a Contact with first name, last name, email, phone, company, job title, street, postal code, city, country and note, so that the Workspace holds complete contact data.
33. As an Editor, I want a Contact to need at least a first name, a last name or an email, so that empty Contacts cannot be saved.
34. As an Editor, I want leading and trailing spaces removed automatically, so that copied text does not create subtle differences.
35. As an Editor, I want invalid emails, unknown country codes and over-long values rejected with an error next to the field, so that I can correct them immediately.
36. As an Editor, I want the form to check obvious mistakes before sending, and to keep what I typed after an error, so that I never retype a form.
37. As an Editor, I want Slovenian characters (č, š, ž, Č, Š, Ž, ć, đ) kept exactly in every field, so that names are spelled correctly.
38. As an Editor, I want to change a Contact, so that its data stays current.
39. As an Editor, I want a change based on an outdated version to be refused, so that I never overwrite a colleague's change without seeing it.
40. As an Editor, I want to delete a Contact without losing it forever, so that a mistake can be undone.
41. As a Member, I want a separate view of Deleted contacts, so that I can find and restore them.

Attributes

42. As an Editor, I want to add free key-value Attributes such as `kompetenca=spletnoProgramiranje`, so that I can record what the Predefined fields do not cover.
43. As an Editor, I want Attributes kept in the order I entered them, so that the Contact reads the way I wrote it.
44. As an Editor, I want keys that are malformed, repeated (ignoring letter case) or equal to a Predefined field name refused, so that Attributes stay consistent and never shadow real fields.
45. As an Editor, I want to change or remove Attributes, so that the Contact stays accurate.

Tags

46. As an Editor, I want to label Contacts with Tags such as `neObvescaj` or `udelezenec2025` by simply typing them, so that I can categorise without setting anything up first.
47. As an Editor, I want Tags that differ only in letter case to be the same Tag, keeping the first spelling, so that categories do not split by accident.
48. As a Member, I want to see the Workspace's Tags with how many Contacts carry each, so that I understand the categories in use.
49. As an Editor, I want to rename a Tag across the whole Workspace, so that a category can be renamed in one step.
50. As an Editor, I want renaming a Tag onto an existing name refused, so that two categories never merge silently.
51. As an Editor, I want to delete a Tag from every Contact at once, so that an obsolete category disappears.
52. As a Member, I want Tag renames and deletions recorded in each affected Contact's history, so that the change is traceable.

Search and filter

53. As a Member, I want one search box that finds Contacts by name, email, phone, company or city, so that finding someone takes one step.
54. As a Member, I want search to ignore letter case and diacritics (`sasa` finds `Saša`), so that I find people however I type.
55. As a Member, I want to filter by one or more Tags, with all or any of them, so that I can work with a category.
56. As a Member, I want to filter by Attribute value or presence, so that I can find, for example, everyone with a given competence.
57. As a Member, I want to filter by country and company, combined with search, so that I can narrow down large lists.
58. As a Member, I want to sort by last name, first name, company or last change, so that the list fits my task.
59. As a Member, I want paging with the total count, so that large Workspaces stay fast and I know how many Contacts match.
60. As a Member, I want search and filters to update the list without reloading the page, so that the application feels quick.

Revisions and Restore

61. As a Member, I want to see every Revision of a Contact with who made it, when and what kind of change it was, so that I know its history.
62. As a Member, I want each Revision to show exactly which fields, Attributes and Tags changed, with old and new values, so that I understand the change at a glance.
63. As an Editor, I want to restore an earlier Revision, so that a wrong change can be undone without retyping.
64. As an Editor, I want a restore to create a new Revision rather than erase history, so that the restore itself is traceable.
65. As an Editor, I want restoring a Revision to bring back Tags that were deleted since, so that the restored state is complete.
66. As an Editor, I want to restore a Deleted contact with its last state, so that deleting is never final by mistake.
67. As a Member, I want Revisions to be impossible to change or delete, so that the audit trail can be trusted.

Duplicates and Merge

68. As a Member, I want to see sets of Contacts that are probably the same person, matched by email, phone or full name, so that I can clean up the Workspace.
69. As a Member, I want email matching to ignore case, phone matching to ignore formatting and `00`/`+`, and name matching to ignore case, extra spaces and diacritics, so that real duplicates are found.
70. As a Member, I want contacts connected through different matches (A and B by email, B and C by phone) shown as one set, so that I merge them in one go.
71. As an Editor, I want a warning, with links, when the Contact I just saved looks like an existing one, so that I notice duplicates immediately without being blocked.
72. As an Editor, I want to Merge 2 to 10 Contacts, choosing which one survives and, per differing value, which value to keep, so that the result is the best data of all.
73. As an Editor, I want Tags and Attributes of merged Contacts combined, so that no categorisation is lost.
74. As an Editor, I want merged-away Contacts kept as Deleted contacts pointing to the Survivor, so that nothing is lost and the merge is traceable.
75. As an Editor, I want a Merge to fail completely if any Contact changed meanwhile, so that I never merge stale data.

Export

76. As a Member, I want to select Contacts with checkboxes and export them to Excel, so that I can hand exactly those on.
77. As a Member, I want to export all Contacts matching my current search and filters when nothing is selected, so that exporting a category takes one click.
78. As a Member, I want the workbook to have a fixed column layout, Tags in one column and one column per Attribute key, so that it is predictable and easy to process.
79. As a Member, I want every cell to be plain text, never a formula, so that opening an export can never run anything.
80. As a Member, I want the file named after the Workspace and the date, so that exports are easy to file.
81. As a Viewer, I want to be allowed to export, so that I can use the data outside the system.

Erasure and privacy

82. As an Owner, I want to permanently erase a Deleted contact with all its Revisions, so that I can honour a person's request to have their data removed.
83. As an Owner, I want only Deleted contacts to be erasable, so that erasure is always a deliberate second step.
84. As a contact person, I want my data never written to logs, so that it does not leak through operations.

Operations

85. As an operator, I want the whole stack (frontend, backend, PostgreSQL, Auth emulator) to start with one command, so that local runs and demonstrations are simple.
86. As an operator, I want data to survive container recreation, so that an update never loses contacts.
87. As an operator, I want health and readiness endpoints used by the containers, so that a broken service is detected.
88. As an operator, I want production to refuse to start with emulator settings or a demo project id, so that test shortcuts can never reach production.
89. As a Member of a Workspace with 10,000 Contacts, I want list and search answers within half a second, so that the application stays pleasant at scale.
90. As a keyboard or screen-reader user, I want the main pages to meet accessibility rules, so that I can use the application too.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Components:** a Spring Boot backend (Java 21) and a React frontend (Vite, React Router, hand-written CSS, no component library) served by nginx, which also forwards `/api` to the backend; PostgreSQL as the only store; Firebase Authentication for sign-in, with the Firebase Auth Emulator in local and test environments; everything started by one Docker Compose file. Exact versions are fixed in the tech stack input; nothing outside it is added without a recorded decision.
- **API:** the REST API is fixed by the API contract input, and its paths, methods, field names and status codes are part of the requirements (the hidden oracle relies on them). Resources: the current User; Workspaces; Members and invitations; Contacts with Revisions, restore and purge; Tags; Duplicate sets; Merge; Export. Errors always have the shape of a list of field errors. Non-Member gets 404 indistinguishable from "does not exist"; insufficient Role gets 403; an outdated version gets 409; over the rate limit 429.
- **Tenancy (ADR-0001):** one shared schema with the Workspace id on every Workspace-owned row. Isolation lives in one Workspace-scoped access layer that receives the Workspace id and the caller's verified membership; no other code reaches the persistence of Workspace-owned data. No row-level security, no schema per Workspace. Checked by an architecture rule.
- **Authentication and authorization:** one authentication adapter verifies the Firebase ID token (signature, audience, issuer, expiry) and yields the User; no other code depends on Firebase. Authorization is the application's own: membership and Role stored in PostgreSQL, never taken from token claims or request bodies. Pending invitations become memberships at the first request with a matching verified email.
- **Revisions:** every create, update, delete, restore and merge writes exactly one immutable Revision per changed Contact, holding the full state (Predefined fields, Attributes, Tags, deleted flag), change type, author and time. The Contact's version is its latest Revision number; changes name the version they are based on (optimistic locking). A change, its Revision and the version check share one transaction; Merge and Tag rename or delete change all affected Contacts in one transaction or none.
- **Deletion:** delete is soft (Deleted contact, restorable); only an Owner's purge of a Deleted contact and Workspace deletion remove data permanently, Revisions included.
- **Duplicates:** exact matching after normalisation (email lower case; phone `00`→`+` and digits only, at least 6 digits; full name lower case, diacritics removed, whitespace collapsed), grouped transitively into Duplicate sets; Deleted contacts excluded. No fuzzy matching.
- **Search:** case- and diacritic-insensitive substring search over name, email, phone, company and city; filters by Tags (all or any), country, company and Attributes; sorting and paging all run in the database, not in memory.
- **Export:** an `.xlsx` workbook with the fixed column order of the contract, one column per Attribute key (lower case, sorted), every cell written as text; at most 10,000 Contacts per Export.
- **Schema:** evolves only through versioned database migrations.
- **Frontend:** Slovenian only, no translation framework; the API's English error messages are mapped to Slovenian texts; no secret in the frontend, its Firebase configuration comes from configuration.
- **Security level:** OWASP ASVS 5.0 Level 2 for both components, plus the project's security requirements (token verification, emulator never in production, isolation, verified-email invitations, rate and size limits, text-only export cells, server-set Revision author, no personal data in logs, text-only rendering, Host header pinning at the proxy, configured CORS).

## Testing Decisions

- **A good test checks external behaviour only:** what a caller of the REST API or a person in the browser can observe (status codes, response bodies, the workbook, what the page shows). Tests never inspect repositories, internal services or table layouts, so the internals can change freely.
- **Seam 1 (primary): the REST API.** All backend acceptance criteria are tested through HTTP against a real PostgreSQL (Testcontainers) with tokens from the Firebase Auth Emulator: Workspaces, Members, isolation (404 with the same body as a missing Workspace), Roles (403), Contacts, Attributes, Tags, search and filters, Revisions and Restore, Duplicate sets, Merge, Export (workbook read back and checked), purge, rate limits. This is the same seam the hidden oracle uses.
- **Token verification in production mode** goes through the same REST seam, with the backend's key endpoint configured to a test key instead of the emulator, covering wrong audience, wrong issuer, expiry and a bad signature (DoD-P05).
- **Seam 2: the frontend's API-client boundary.** UI criteria (field errors next to fields with values kept, the duplicate warning with links, controls hidden by Role, selection and Export, the history diff, search and filters without reload) are component tests with the API client faked.
- **Seam 3: the browser against the full stack,** exactly the seven fixed end-to-end scenarios E2E-01 to E2E-07, each also running an axe-core accessibility check on the main pages it visits. No other end-to-end tests.
- **Acceptance tests come first and are frozen** (template phase 3); unit tests are added only afterwards to reach the quality gate: line coverage ≥ 95 % and adjusted mutation score ≥ 90 % per component, over all production code.
- **Runtime demonstrations, not tests:** persistence across container recreation, health and readiness, and the 10,000-Contact response-time target.
- **Prior art:** none in this repository yet (no code). The closest prior art is the conference-registration project built with the same template: Testcontainers-based acceptance tests through MockMvc, Vitest component tests, Playwright end-to-end tests, PIT and Stryker for mutation.

## Out of Scope

- Import of Contacts from Excel, CSV, vCard or any other source (a candidate change request).
- Fuzzy or similarity-based duplicate matching; automatic merging.
- Sending any email, including invitations and notifications.
- Typed Attributes, a Workspace-wide Attribute schema, several values per Attribute key.
- Moving or copying Contacts between Workspaces; sharing a single Contact outside its Workspace.
- A Workspace-wide activity feed (a candidate change request).
- Translations other than Slovenian; multi-factor authentication; roles from identity-provider claims.
- Database-level tenant isolation (row-level security, schema per Workspace), per ADR-0001.
- An administration interface across Workspaces; mobile applications; payment.

## Further Notes

- The requirements are deliberately fixed so that agent runs are comparable: the acceptance criteria, end-to-end scenarios and API contract are inputs that the implementer does not reword, and a gap or contradiction is recorded as a decision rather than resolved silently.
- A hidden oracle outside this repository checks every finished run through the API; implementers never see it and must not try to.
- Manual checks left for a human after release: sign-up, email verification and Google sign-in against a real Firebase project; HTTPS, redirects and `/api` routing behind the production reverse proxy.
- The domain vocabulary (Workspace, Member, Role, Contact, Predefined field, Attribute, Tag, Revision, Deleted contact, Restore, Duplicate set, Merge, Survivor, Export) is defined in the glossary; avoided synonyms (group, project, tenant, record, version in prose, custom field, label, archive, master) are not used in code, API or UI.

### #2 Walking skeleton: sign in and see my Workspaces
## Parent

#1

## What to build

A User can open the application, sign up or sign in (email and password, or Google, through Firebase Authentication; the Auth emulator locally), see the list of Workspaces they belong to, create one and rename it as Owner, and sign out. The whole stack (frontend, backend, PostgreSQL, Auth emulator) starts with one Compose command. The backend verifies every token itself, keeps its own User record, and reaches Workspace data only through the Workspace-scoped access layer of ADR-0001, so a non-Member gets 404. Health and readiness, rate and size limits, security headers and the production start-up guard are in place from the first slice.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC-001-01: requests without a valid token (none, malformed, expired, other project) get 401 and no data
- [ ] AC-001-02, AC-001-03: `GET /api/me` creates the User record once and keeps email, verified flag and display name current
- [ ] AC-001-04: sign-up, sign-in and sign-out work in the browser; after sign-out every page shows the sign-in page
- [ ] AC-002-01..03: creating a Workspace makes the creator Owner; empty, whitespace-only or over-long names are rejected (400, `name`); the list shows only the caller's Workspaces with their Role
- [ ] A non-Member of a Workspace gets 404, identical to a Workspace that does not exist
- [ ] SR-02, DoD-P06: the production profile refuses to start with the emulator setting, a `demo-` project id or an empty project id
- [ ] SR-05, NFR-04: rate limit (429) and body size limit (413) are active; health and readiness are used by the container health checks
- [ ] `docker compose up` from a clean checkout starts the stack as the API contract describes (ports, emulator by default)


### #3 Members, invitations and Roles
## Parent

#1

## What to build

An Owner shares a Workspace: adds people by email with a Role (Owner, Editor, Viewer), sees Members and pending invitations, changes Roles, removes Members and cancels invitations; any Member can leave. A person who has not signed up yet gets a pending invitation that becomes a membership at their first request with that verified email. A Workspace always keeps at least one Owner. Every action a Role does not allow is answered with 403, and the UI hides those controls.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC-003-01: adding an existing verified User (any letter case) makes them a Member at once
- [ ] AC-003-02, AC-003-03: a pending invitation activates only for a matching verified email, then disappears
- [ ] AC-003-04: adding a Member or invited person again is rejected (409)
- [ ] AC-003-05, AC-003-06: the last Owner cannot leave, be removed or be demoted (409); with two Owners a demotion works and takes the Owner rights away
- [ ] AC-003-07: a Member who leaves no longer sees the Workspace (404)
- [ ] AC-003-08, AC-002-04: Editors and Viewers cannot manage Members or rename the Workspace (403)
- [ ] AC-003-09: a cancelled invitation never grants access
- [ ] Members page in the UI; controls not allowed by the Role are not shown


### #4 Contacts with Predefined fields, Revisions and version checks
## Parent

#1

## What to build

An Editor creates, views, changes and deletes Contacts with the Predefined fields (first name, last name, email, phone, company, job title, street, postal code, city, country, note). Every change writes an immutable Revision and must name the version it was based on, so a lost update is refused with 409. Deleting makes a Deleted contact, hidden from the list but kept with its Revisions. Viewers can read but change nothing. The form checks obvious mistakes before sending and shows the backend's field errors next to the fields, keeping what was typed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC-005-01: a valid Contact is created (201) with version 1 and every value stored
- [ ] AC-005-02: a Contact without first name, last name and email is rejected (400)
- [ ] AC-005-03: leading and trailing spaces are removed; a value of only spaces becomes absent
- [ ] AC-005-04: invalid email, unknown country code or over-long values are rejected with the field's error; a lower-case country is stored in upper case
- [ ] AC-005-05: Slovenian characters survive unchanged
- [ ] AC-005-06: an update naming the current version is applied and increments it; an outdated version gets 409 and changes nothing
- [ ] AC-005-07: delete gives 204, hides the Contact, `GET` shows it as deleted and a `DELETE` Revision is added
- [ ] AC-005-08: a Viewer cannot create, update, delete or restore (403)
- [ ] AC-005-09: the form shows field errors next to the fields, sends nothing when invalid, and keeps the values after a backend rejection


### #5 Attributes on Contacts
## Parent

#1

## What to build

An Editor adds free key-value Attributes to a Contact (`kompetenca=spletnoProgramiranje`), changes and removes them in the Contact form. Keys follow the key rule, are unique on the Contact ignoring letter case and never shadow a Predefined field, `id` or `tags`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC-006-01: Attributes are stored and returned in the order given
- [ ] AC-006-02: a key outside the pattern is rejected (400, `attributes[i].key`)
- [ ] AC-006-03: two keys differing only in letter case are rejected for the second one
- [ ] AC-006-04: a key equal to a Predefined field name, `id` or `tags` (any case) is rejected
- [ ] AC-006-05: empty or over-long values and more than 100 Attributes are rejected
- [ ] AC-006-06: an update replaces the Attributes as given


### #6 Tags
## Parent

#1

## What to build

An Editor labels Contacts with Tags by typing them; a new Tag is created on first use and reused regardless of letter case, keeping the first spelling. Members see the Workspace's Tags with how many active Contacts carry each. An Editor renames or deletes a Tag across the Workspace in one step, which writes a Revision on every affected Contact. Ends with end-to-end scenario E2E-01 (first Contact in a new Workspace).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC-007-01, AC-007-02: Tags are created implicitly and reused case-insensitively; counts are correct
- [ ] AC-007-03: invalid Tags (space, too long, repeated on one Contact, more than 50) are rejected (400)
- [ ] AC-007-04: rename updates every Contact and writes an `UPDATE` Revision on each
- [ ] AC-007-05: renaming onto an existing name (any case) is rejected (409)
- [ ] AC-007-06: delete removes the Tag from every Contact with a Revision each
- [ ] AC-007-07: a Viewer cannot rename or delete Tags (403)
- [ ] E2E-01 passes, including its accessibility check


### #7 Search, filter, sort and paging
## Parent

#1

## What to build

A Member finds Contacts with one search box (name, email, phone, company, city; ignoring letter case and diacritics, so `sasa` finds `Saša`) and narrows the list by Tags (all or any), Attributes (value or presence), country and company. The list sorts, pages with a total count, and updates without a page reload. Everything runs in the database (AR-10). A separate view lists only Deleted contacts.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC-008-01, AC-008-02: search ignores case and diacritics and covers exactly the listed fields
- [ ] AC-008-03: Tag filters with `all` and `any`
- [ ] AC-008-04: Attribute filters by `key=value` (case-insensitive) and by `key`
- [ ] AC-008-05: country, company and search text combine with AND
- [ ] AC-008-06: paging with total and no repeats; `size` above 100 is rejected
- [ ] AC-008-07: Deleted contacts only in the Deleted view
- [ ] AC-008-08: the list page filters without a reload and shows the total


### #8 Revision history and Restore
## Parent

#1

## What to build

A Member opens a Contact's history and sees every Revision with author, time, change type and exactly which fields, Attributes and Tags changed. An Editor restores an earlier Revision (writing a new `RESTORE` Revision, bringing back Tags deleted since) or restores a Deleted contact. Revisions can never be changed or deleted. Ends with E2E-04.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC-009-01: Revisions are listed newest first with number, type, author and full state
- [ ] AC-009-02: restoring Revision 1 writes Revision n+1 equal to it and leaves the others unchanged
- [ ] AC-009-03: restoring brings back a Tag that was deleted from the Workspace since
- [ ] AC-009-04: a Deleted contact is restored with its last state; restoring one of its Revisions before that is rejected (409)
- [ ] AC-009-05: of two concurrent saves on the same version exactly one wins
- [ ] AC-009-06, AC-009-07: the history page shows differences, restore works for Editors and is hidden for Viewers
- [ ] AC-009-08: no endpoint changes or deletes a Revision
- [ ] E2E-04 passes


### #9 Duplicate detection and save-time warning
## Parent

#1

## What to build

A Member sees Duplicate sets in a Duplicates page: active Contacts matching by normalised email, phone or full name, grouped transitively. Saving a Contact that matches an existing one still succeeds but returns its possible duplicates, and the form shows a warning with links to them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC-010-01: emails match ignoring letter case
- [ ] AC-010-02: phones match ignoring formatting and `00`/`+`; fewer than 6 digits never match
- [ ] AC-010-03: full names match ignoring case, extra spaces and diacritics; a first name alone never matches
- [ ] AC-010-04: matches are grouped transitively, with every match kind listed
- [ ] AC-010-05: Deleted contacts leave their sets
- [ ] AC-010-06: create and update return `possibleDuplicates` without blocking the save
- [ ] AC-010-07: the form shows the warning with links and the Contact stays saved


### #10 Merge
## Parent

#1

## What to build

An Editor merges 2 to 10 active Contacts: picks the Survivor and, for each differing value, which Contact it comes from. Tags and Attributes are combined; the others become Deleted contacts pointing to the Survivor; every affected Contact gets a Revision; the whole Merge fails if any Contact changed meanwhile. The Duplicates page offers it as a dialog. Ends with E2E-05.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC-011-01..03: default and chosen sources for fields and Attributes, Tags and Attributes combined
- [ ] AC-011-04: the others become Deleted contacts with `mergedInto` and a `MERGED_AWAY` Revision; the Survivor gets `MERGE`
- [ ] AC-011-05: invalid requests (count, repeats, Survivor or source not listed, Deleted contact) are rejected (400)
- [ ] AC-011-06: any outdated version rejects the whole Merge (409) and changes nothing
- [ ] AC-011-07: the merge dialog works from the Duplicates page
- [ ] AC-011-08: Viewers cannot merge (403)
- [ ] E2E-05 passes


### #11 Excel Export
## Parent

#1

## What to build

A Member exports either the Contacts they selected with checkboxes or, with nothing selected, all Contacts matching the current search and filters, as an `.xlsx` workbook named after the Workspace and the date. The column layout is fixed by the API contract, with one column per Attribute key; every cell is text, never a formula. Viewers may export. Ends with E2E-02 and E2E-07.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC-012-01, AC-012-02: selection and filter exports contain exactly the right Contacts in the right order
- [ ] AC-012-03: fixed columns in contract order, then Attribute columns (lower case, sorted), Tags joined by `, `
- [ ] AC-012-04: Slovenian characters and values starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@` are exported unchanged as text
- [ ] AC-012-05: both or neither of selection and filter, a Deleted or foreign Contact, or more than 10,000 Contacts are rejected (400)
- [ ] AC-012-06: selection and export in the list page download the named file
- [ ] AC-012-07: Viewers can export
- [ ] E2E-02 and E2E-07 pass


### #12 Permanent erasure and Workspace deletion
## Parent

#1

## What to build

An Owner permanently erases a Deleted contact together with all its Revisions (the erasure path for a person's request), and deletes a whole Workspace after typing its exact name, removing all its Contacts, Revisions, Tags, memberships and invitations.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC-013-01: purging a Deleted contact gives 204; afterwards the Contact and its Revisions answer 404 and no row remains
- [ ] AC-013-02: purging an active Contact is rejected (409)
- [ ] AC-013-03: Editors and Viewers cannot purge (403)
- [ ] AC-002-05: deleting a Workspace with the exact name gives 204 and every former Member gets 404 for it and its Contacts
- [ ] AC-002-06: a wrong `confirmName` is rejected (400)


### #13 Isolation audit and Viewer journey
## Parent

#1

## What to build

With every endpoint in place, prove that Workspaces are fully isolated: a non-Member gets a 404 identical to a missing Workspace on every endpoint, a Contact is unreachable through another Workspace's path, and search, Tags, Duplicate sets and Exports never mix Workspaces. An architecture rule enforces that Workspace-owned data is reached only through the Workspace-scoped access layer. Ends with E2E-03 (isolation) and E2E-06 (Viewer invited before sign-up).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC-004-01: every Workspace endpoint answers a non-Member with 404, same body as for a Workspace that does not exist
- [ ] AC-004-02: a Contact cannot be read or changed through another Workspace's path
- [ ] AC-004-03: lists, Tag counts, Duplicate sets and filter Exports never include another Workspace's data
- [ ] AC-004-04: a non-Member opening a Workspace or Contact URL sees a not-found page and no data
- [ ] AC-004-05: ids, Roles or authors in request bodies never widen access
- [ ] AR-04: the architecture rule for the Workspace-scoped access layer passes
- [ ] E2E-03 and E2E-06 pass


### #14 Scale and accessibility
## Parent

#1

## What to build

The application stays pleasant at scale and usable for everyone: with 10,000 Contacts in one Workspace, list, search and filter answer within 500 ms at the 95th percentile and an Export of all of them within 10 s; data survives recreation of every container; the main pages have no serious or critical accessibility violations and work with the keyboard alone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] NFR-07: runtime demonstration with seeded data meets the response-time and Export targets
- [ ] NFR-02: data is still present after `docker compose down` and `up`
- [ ] NFR-06: axe-core reports no serious or critical violations on the Workspace list, Contact list, Contact page, history page and Duplicates page; all are keyboard-usable

# API contract

All endpoints live under `/api`, take and return JSON (except the Export workbook), and need `Authorization: Bearer <Firebase ID token>` (except `/api/health*`).

## Ports (Docker Compose)

| Service | Host port | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| frontend (nginx) | 8080 | serves the UI, forwards `/api` to the backend |
| backend | 8081 | Spring Boot; also reachable directly for API tests |
| auth (Firebase Auth Emulator) | 9099 | used by default; project id `demo-contacts` |
| db (PostgreSQL 16) | not published | volume `db-data` |

## Errors

Every error body is a list of field errors:

```json
{ "errors": [ { "field": "email", "message": "must be a valid email" } ] }
```

`field` is `null` for errors that belong to no field. Status codes:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 400 | validation error; `field` names the offending field (`name`, `email`, `attributes[2].key`, `tags[0]`, ...) |
| 401 | missing, malformed, expired or foreign token |
| 403 | the caller's Role does not allow the action |
| 404 | not found, **or the caller is not a Member** (identical body: `{"errors":[{"field":null,"message":"not found"}]}`) |
| 409 | outdated `version`, duplicate Member, last Owner, Tag name taken, purge of an active Contact, Restore of a stale Revision |
| 413 | request body larger than 1 MB |
| 429 | rate limit (per User, default 300 requests per minute) |

## User

`GET /api/me` → 200 `{ id, email, emailVerified, displayName }`. Creates the User on first call, updates email, verified flag and display name from the token on every call, and activates pending invitations for a verified email.

## Workspaces

| Method and path | Role | Body | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/workspaces` | any User | | 200 `[{ id, name, role }]` sorted by name |
| `POST /api/workspaces` | any User | `{ name }` (1–100 chars after trimming) | 201 `{ id, name, role: "OWNER" }` |
| `GET /api/workspaces/{wid}` | Member | | 200 `{ id, name, role }` |
| `PATCH /api/workspaces/{wid}` | Owner | `{ name }` | 200 `{ id, name, role }` |
| `DELETE /api/workspaces/{wid}` | Owner | `{ confirmName }` (must equal the name exactly, else 400 `confirmName`) | 204 |

Roles: `OWNER`, `EDITOR`, `VIEWER`.

## Members and invitations

| Method and path | Role | Body | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/workspaces/{wid}/members` | Member | | 200 `{ members: [{ userId, email, displayName, role }], invitations: [{ id, email, role, createdAt }] }` |
| `POST /api/workspaces/{wid}/members` | Owner | `{ email, role }` | 201 `{ status: "MEMBER", member: {...} }` for a verified existing User, otherwise 201 `{ status: "INVITED", invitation: {...} }`; 409 if already a Member or invited |
| `PATCH /api/workspaces/{wid}/members/{userId}` | Owner | `{ role }` | 200 member; 409 when it would leave no Owner |
| `DELETE /api/workspaces/{wid}/members/{userId}` | Owner, or the Member themself (leave) | | 204; 409 when it would leave no Owner |
| `DELETE /api/workspaces/{wid}/invitations/{id}` | Owner | | 204 |

## Contacts

Contact body:

```json
{
  "id": "uuid", "version": 3, "deleted": false, "mergedInto": null,
  "firstName": "Saša", "lastName": "Novak", "email": "sasa@example.si", "phone": "+386 41 123 456",
  "company": "Podjetje d.o.o.", "jobTitle": "Vodja", "street": "Slovenska 1", "postalCode": "1000",
  "city": "Ljubljana", "country": "SI", "note": "...",
  "attributes": [ { "key": "kompetenca", "value": "spletnoProgramiranje" } ],
  "tags": [ "udelezenec2025" ],
  "createdAt": "...", "updatedAt": "..."
}
```

Field rules: values are trimmed, a blank value becomes `null`. At least one of `firstName`, `lastName`, `email` (400, field `firstName`). Maximum lengths: `firstName`, `lastName`, `city` 100; `email` 254 (must be a valid address); `phone` 50; `company`, `jobTitle`, `street` 200; `postalCode` 20; `note` 2000. `country` is an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, stored in upper case.

Attributes: at most 100; `key` matches `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,49}$`, unique on the Contact ignoring case, not equal (ignoring case) to a Predefined field name, `id` or `tags`; `value` 1–500 characters after trimming. Order is kept. Errors name `attributes[i].key` / `attributes[i].value`.

Tags: at most 50 per Contact; each 1–50 characters with no whitespace; no repeats on one Contact ignoring case (errors name `tags[i]`). A new Tag is created on first use; an existing one is reused regardless of case and keeps its first spelling.

| Method and path | Role | Body / query | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/workspaces/{wid}/contacts` | Member | query below | 200 `{ items: [Contact], total, page, size }` |
| `POST /api/workspaces/{wid}/contacts` | Editor | Contact fields, `attributes`, `tags` | 201 Contact + `possibleDuplicates: [{ id, firstName, lastName, email, phone, matchKinds }]` |
| `GET /api/workspaces/{wid}/contacts/{cid}` | Member | | 200 Contact (also a Deleted contact) |
| `PUT /api/workspaces/{wid}/contacts/{cid}` | Editor | `version` + all fields | 200 Contact + `possibleDuplicates`; 409 on outdated `version` |
| `DELETE /api/workspaces/{wid}/contacts/{cid}?version=n` | Editor | (`version` optional) | 204, writes a `DELETE` Revision |
| `POST /api/workspaces/{wid}/contacts/{cid}/restore` | Editor | | 200 Contact; restores a Deleted contact with its last state (`RESTORE` Revision); 409 if not deleted |
| `POST /api/workspaces/{wid}/contacts/{cid}/purge` | Owner | | 204; permanently removes a Deleted contact and its Revisions; 409 for an active Contact |
| `GET /api/workspaces/{wid}/contacts/{cid}/revisions` | Member | | 200 `[Revision]` newest first |
| `POST /api/workspaces/{wid}/contacts/{cid}/revisions/{n}/restore` | Editor | `{ version }` | 200 Contact; writes a `RESTORE` Revision equal to Revision n; 409 on outdated version or for a Deleted contact |

List query: `q` (search text, case and diacritic insensitive, over first name, last name, full name, email, phone, company, city), `tag` (repeatable), `tagMode=all|any` (default `all`), `attr` (repeatable, `key=value` matches value case-insensitively, `key` alone means presence), `country`, `company` (case-insensitive equality), `deleted=true` (Deleted contacts only; default active only), `sort=lastName|firstName|company|updatedAt` (default `lastName`), `dir=asc|desc` (default `asc`, `desc` for `updatedAt`), `page` (from 0), `size` (1–100, default 20; above 100 → 400 `size`).

Revision: `{ number, type, author: { id, email, displayName }, createdAt, state: { firstName, ..., note, attributes, tags, deleted, mergedInto } }`. Types: `CREATE`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `RESTORE`, `MERGE`, `MERGED_AWAY`. No endpoint changes or deletes a Revision (only purge and Workspace deletion remove them with their Contact).

## Tags

| Method and path | Role | Body | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/workspaces/{wid}/tags` | Member | | 200 `[{ name, count }]` sorted by name; `count` = active Contacts |
| `PATCH /api/workspaces/{wid}/tags/{name}` | Editor | `{ name }` | 200 `{ name, count }`; `UPDATE` Revision on every affected Contact; 409 if the new name exists (any case, other Tag) |
| `DELETE /api/workspaces/{wid}/tags/{name}` | Editor | | 204; `UPDATE` Revision on every affected Contact |

`{name}` is matched ignoring case.

## Duplicate sets

`GET /api/workspaces/{wid}/duplicate-sets` (Member) → 200 `[{ contacts: [Contact], matches: [{ contactIds, kind: "EMAIL" | "PHONE" | "NAME", value }] }]`; each match lists every Contact of the set sharing that normalised value.

Normalisation: email lower case; phone `00`→`+`, then digits only, at least 6 digits; full name = first + last name, lower case, diacritics removed, whitespace collapsed (both names needed). Active Contacts only, grouped transitively.

## Merge

`POST /api/workspaces/{wid}/merge` (Editor)

```json
{
  "survivorId": "uuid",
  "contacts": [ { "id": "uuid", "version": 2 }, { "id": "uuid", "version": 5 } ],
  "fieldSources": { "email": "uuid-of-source" },
  "attributeSources": { "kompetenca": "uuid-of-source" }
}
```

2–10 distinct active Contacts; the Survivor and every source must be among them (400 otherwise). For a field without a chosen source the Survivor's value is kept, or the first non-empty value in list order when the Survivor has none. Attributes are combined by key (ignoring case); the Survivor's value wins unless `attributeSources` names another Contact. Tags are combined. The others become Deleted contacts with `mergedInto` = Survivor and a `MERGED_AWAY` Revision; the Survivor gets a `MERGE` Revision. Any outdated version → 409 and nothing changes. Response 200: the Survivor.

## Export

`POST /api/workspaces/{wid}/export` (Member) with exactly one of:

- `{ "contactIds": ["uuid", ...] }`: those Contacts, in list default order (last name, first name); a Deleted, foreign or unknown id → 400 `contactIds`;
- `{ "filter": { q, tag, tagMode, attr, country, company, sort, dir } }`: every active Contact matching, in the filter's order.

Both or neither → 400. More than 10,000 Contacts → 400. Response 200 `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<ascii-name>-<yyyy-MM-dd>.xlsx"; filename*=UTF-8''<name>-<yyyy-MM-dd>.xlsx` (spaces become `-`; the name keeps only letters, digits, `-` and `_`; the plain form drops diacritics; the date is in Europe/Ljubljana).

Columns, in order: `Ime`, `Priimek`, `E-pošta`, `Telefon`, `Podjetje`, `Delovno mesto`, `Ulica`, `Poštna številka`, `Kraj`, `Država`, `Opomba`, `Oznake` (Tags joined by `, `), then one column per Attribute key (lower case, sorted). Every cell is a text cell; values are never formulas.

## Health

`GET /api/health` (liveness) and `GET /api/health/ready` (readiness, checks the database), no token needed.

```json
  "fieldSources": { "email": "uuid-of-source" },
  "attributeSources": { "kompetenca": "uuid-of-source" }
}
```

2–10 distinct active Contacts; the Survivor and every source must be among them (400 otherwise). For a field without a chosen source the Survivor's value is kept, or the first non-empty value in list order when the Survivor has none. Attributes are combined by key (ignoring case); the Survivor's value wins unless `attributeSources` names another Contact. Tags are combined. The others become Deleted contacts with `mergedInto` = Survivor and a `MERGED_AWAY` Revision; the Survivor gets a `MERGE` Revision. Any outdated version → 409 and nothing changes. Response 200: the Survivor.

## Export

`POST /api/workspaces/{wid}/export` (Member) with exactly one of:

- `{ "contactIds": ["uuid", ...] }`: those Contacts, in list default order (last name, first name); a Deleted, foreign or unknown id → 400 `contactIds`;
- `{ "filter": { q, tag, tagMode, attr, country, company, sort, dir } }`: every active Contact matching, in the filter's order.

Both or neither → 400. More than 10,000 Contacts → 400. Response 200 `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<ascii-name>-<yyyy-MM-dd>.xlsx"; filename*=UTF-8''<name>-<yyyy-MM-dd>.xlsx` (spaces become `-`; the name keeps only letters, digits, `-` and `_`; the plain form drops diacritics; the date is in Europe/Ljubljana).

Columns, in order: `Ime`, `Priimek`, `E-pošta`, `Telefon`, `Podjetje`, `Delovno mesto`, `Ulica`, `Poštna številka`, `Kraj`, `Država`, `Opomba`, `Oznake` (Tags joined by `, `), then one column per Attribute key (lower case, sorted). Every cell is a text cell; values are never formulas.

## Health

`GET /api/health` (liveness) and `GET /api/health/ready` (readiness, checks the database), no token needed.

 # Contact Management
 
-A deliberately simple CRM for one organization: it stores Contacts, labels them with Tags and custom Attributes, keeps a full history of every change, and exports them to Excel.
+A deliberately simple, multi-tenant contact manager: people keep the Contacts of one project or company in a Workspace, label them with Tags and Attributes, see every change as a Revision, find Duplicate sets, Merge them and Export to Excel.
 
-## People
-
-**Contact**:
-A person the organization keeps data about. Has predefined fields (first name, last name, one email, one phone, one address, country, company) plus any number of Attributes and Tags.
-_Avoid_: User (for records), person, customer, entry, record
+## People and access
 
 **User**:
-Someone who signs in to the system and works with Contacts.
-_Avoid_: Contact, account, member
+Someone who signs in (Firebase Authentication) and is known to the application by their sign-in identity.
+_Avoid_: account, member (for the person in general)
 
-**Company**:
-A plain text field on a Contact naming where they work; not a thing in its own right.
-_Avoid_: Organization, account
+**Workspace**:
+The container for the Contacts of one project or company. Only its Members see it; nothing in it is visible from another Workspace.
+_Avoid_: group, project, tenant, organization
 
-## Access
+**Member**:
+A User who belongs to a Workspace with exactly one Role there.
+_Avoid_: participant, collaborator
 
 **Role**:
-What a User may do. Every User has exactly one Role, and it applies to all Contacts:
-- **Viewer** browses, searches and Exports.
-- **Editor** also creates, edits, Tags, Archives, Restores and Merges.
-- **Admin** also manages Users, Tags and Attribute Keys, and Erases Contacts.
-_Avoid_: Permission level, group
+What a Member may do in one Workspace:
+- **Viewer** reads, searches and Exports.
+- **Editor** also creates, changes, deletes, Restores and Merges Contacts and renames or deletes Tags.
+- **Owner** also manages Members and invitations, renames and deletes the Workspace and purges Deleted contacts.
+
+A Workspace always has at least one Owner.
+_Avoid_: permission level, admin
 
 **Invitation**:
-An Admin adding someone's email so they can sign in. Only invited emails get access.
-_Avoid_: Registration, sign-up
+A pending Membership for an email that has no User yet. It becomes a Membership at the first request of a User with that verified email.
+_Avoid_: registration, sign-up
 
-**Deactivation**:
-Removing a User's access. The User is never deleted, and their name stays on every Version they made.
-_Avoid_: Delete user, remove user
+## Contacts
 
-## Labelling
+**Contact**:
+A person the Workspace keeps data about: Predefined fields, Attributes and Tags.
+_Avoid_: record, entry, customer
 
-**Tag**:
-A short label without a value (e.g. `doNotNotify`, `participant2025`) that puts a Contact in a category. Tags come from one shared list, a Contact can have any number, and no Tag has meaning built into the system.
-_Avoid_: Label, category, group
+**Predefined field**:
+One of the fixed fields of a Contact: first name, last name, email, phone, company, job title, street, postal code, city, country, note.
+_Avoid_: column, property
 
 **Attribute**:
-A custom key–value pair on a Contact (e.g. `competence=webProgramming`). The value is always text.
-_Avoid_: Custom field, property
+A free key–value pair on a Contact (e.g. `kompetenca=spletnoProgramiranje`). The value is always text; keys are unique on a Contact ignoring letter case.
+_Avoid_: custom field, property
 
-**Attribute Key**:
-An entry in the shared catalog of keys that Attributes use; it is added the first time someone uses it.

content.content:
# Single-tenant: one deployment serves one organization

The product is meant to compete with other CRMs, which are usually multi-tenant SaaS. Even so, each deployment serves exactly one organization: all Users see the same Contacts, Tags and Attribute Keys, and duplicate detection covers the whole database. We chose this to keep the data model, authorization and queries simple for v1, in line with the product's main selling point of being easy to use. If another organization needs the system, it gets its own deployment and its own database. Moving to true multi-tenancy later would mean adding an organization boundary to every table, query and permission check.
# ADR-0001: Workspaces in one shared schema, isolated by one access layer

Status: accepted (supersedes the earlier single-tenant draft, per spec #1)

Each project or company is a Workspace in one deployment. All Workspace-owned rows (Contacts, Attributes, Tags, Revisions, memberships, invitations) live in one shared PostgreSQL schema and carry the Workspace id.

Isolation lives in one Workspace-scoped access layer. `WorkspaceAccess` is the only code that turns a Workspace id and the caller into a `WorkspaceScope`, and it does so only after reading the caller's membership from PostgreSQL. Every store of Workspace-owned data takes a `WorkspaceScope` as its first parameter and filters by its Workspace id. A non-Member gets the same 404 as for a Workspace that does not exist. An ArchUnit rule (`ArchitectureTest`) enforces that only the store package touches JDBC, that every store method takes a `WorkspaceScope`, and that only `WorkspaceAccess` creates one.

Rejected: row-level security and schema per Workspace. They are stronger, but they make migrations, connection handling and tests heavier than this simple product needs.

**SPEC conformance review, d13ae39..HEAD**

I found no serious defects in the main areas. Membership checks, 404-for-non-Member (same body), 403 role checks, the version check inside the UPDATE statement (409), Revision append, Merge and Tag operations in one transaction, Workspace-filtered stores and the ArchUnit rule all match the contract. The findings below are mostly partial work and edge cases.

**(a) Missing or partial**
1. The quality gate is not set up. Spec: "line coverage ≥ 95 % and adjusted mutation score ≥ 90 % per component". `backend/pom.xml` has no JaCoCo or PIT, and `frontend/package.json` has no Stryker or coverage script.
2. Tokens in backend tests are hand-built, not taken from the emulator. Spec: "tested through HTTP against a real PostgreSQL (Testcontainers) with tokens from the Firebase Auth Emulator". You already knew this. It is a deviation from the spec, and the unsigned-token path in `TokenVerifier` is only checked against itself.

**(b) Scope creep (small)**
3. `ContactSearchStore.possibleDuplicates` stops at `LIMIT 20`. The contract says "create and update return `possibleDuplicates`" with no cap, so matches beyond 20 are silently dropped.
4. `GLOSSARY.md` was rewritten and the received single-tenant ADR was replaced. Spec: "the glossary and ADR-0001 … the implementer does not reword". It is recorded as superseding the earlier draft "per spec #1", so it is defensible, but it is still a rewrite of inputs.

**(c) Implemented but looks wrong**
5. Some wrong query parameters get 404 instead of 400. Spec: "400 | validation error; `field` names the offending field". `ErrorHandler` maps every `MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException` to 404. So `DELETE …/contacts/{cid}?version=abc` returns 404.
6. A very large `page` causes a 500. Spec: "`page` (from 0)". `ContactQuery` checks only `page < 0`, although its error message says "between 0 and 100000". `page * size` is an `int`, so a large `page` overflows to a negative OFFSET and PostgreSQL fails.
7. Tag rename and delete also write `UPDATE` Revisions on Deleted contacts (`TagStore.contactsWith` says "active or deleted"). Spec: "writes a Revision on every affected Contact". This is a reading of the spec, not clearly a bug, but a hidden-oracle Revision count on Deleted contacts could differ.
8. A restored Revision can differ from Revision n. Spec: "restoring Revision 1 writes Revision n+1 equal to it". `ContactService.write` looks Tags up again by lower-case name. If the original Tag was deleted and another Tag with the same letters in a different case exists, the new Revision gets the existing spelling, not the one in Revision n.
9. Rate limiting never counts requests that fail sign-in. Spec: "rate limit (429)". The `RateLimiter` filter (order 4) runs after `AuthFilter` (order 3), so its per-address fallback is never reached and floods of bad tokens are not limited. The contract asks for a per-User limit, so this is a gap in protection rather than a contract break.
10. A non-Member can get 400 instead of 404 on endpoints with a JSON body. Spec: "every Workspace endpoint answers a non-Member with 404". Spring reads the body before `access.open` runs, so a non-Member sending a malformed body gets 400. A missing Workspace gets the same 400, so nothing leaks, but the 404 rule is not met for those requests.

**SPEC conformance review, d13ae39..HEAD**

I found no serious defects in the main areas. Membership checks, 404-for-non-Member (same body), 403 role checks, the version check inside the UPDATE statement (409), Revision append, Merge and Tag operations in one transaction, Workspace-filtered stores and the ArchUnit rule all match the contract. The findings below are mostly partial work and edge cases.

**(a) Missing or partial**
1. The quality gate is not set up. Spec: "line coverage ≥ 95 % and adjusted mutation score ≥ 90 % per component". `backend/pom.xml` has no JaCoCo or PIT, and `frontend/package.json` has no Stryker or coverage script.
2. Tokens in backend tests are hand-built, not taken from the emulator. Spec: "tested through HTTP against a real PostgreSQL (Testcontainers) with tokens from the Firebase Auth Emulator". You already knew this. It is a deviation from the spec, and the unsigned-token path in `TokenVerifier` is only checked against itself.

**(b) Scope creep (small)**
3. `ContactSearchStore.possibleDuplicates` stops at `LIMIT 20`. The contract says "create and update return `possibleDuplicates`" with no cap, so matches beyond 20 are silently dropped.
4. `GLOSSARY.md` was rewritten and the received single-tenant ADR was replaced. Spec: "the glossary and ADR-0001 … the implementer does not reword". It is recorded as superseding the earlier draft "per spec #1", so it is defensible, but it is still a rewrite of inputs.

**(c) Implemented but looks wrong**
5. Some wrong query parameters get 404 instead of 400. Spec: "400 | validation error; `field` names the offending field". `ErrorHandler` maps every `MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException` to 404. So `DELETE …/contacts/{cid}?version=abc` returns 404.
6. A very large `page` causes a 500. Spec: "`page` (from 0)". `ContactQuery` checks only `page < 0`, although its error message says "between 0 and 100000". `page * size` is an `int`, so a large `page` overflows to a negative OFFSET and PostgreSQL fails.
7. Tag rename and delete also write `UPDATE` Revisions on Deleted contacts (`TagStore.contactsWith` says "active or deleted"). Spec: "writes a Revision on every affected Contact". This is a reading of the spec, not clearly a bug, but a hidden-oracle Revision count on Deleted contacts could differ.
8. A restored Revision can differ from Revision n. Spec: "restoring Revision 1 writes Revision n+1 equal to it". `ContactService.write` looks Tags up again by lower-case name. If the original Tag was deleted and another Tag with the same letters in a different case exists, the new Revision gets the existing spelling, not the one in Revision n.
9. Rate limiting never counts requests that fail sign-in. Spec: "rate limit (429)". The `RateLimiter` filter (order 4) runs after `AuthFilter` (order 3), so its per-address fallback is never reached and floods of bad tokens are not limited. The contract asks for a per-User limit, so this is a gap in protection rather than a contract break.
10. A non-Member can get 400 instead of 404 on endpoints with a JSON body. Spec: "every Workspace endpoint answers a non-Member with 404". Spring reads the body before `access.open` runs, so a non-Member sending a malformed body gets 400. A missing Workspace gets the same 400, so nothing leaks, but the 404 rule is not met for those requests.
